articles.title: Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd break their silence on relationship in new UConn documentary
articles.summary: Dallas Wings stars Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd are publicly discussing their romantic relationship for the first time since becoming WNBA teammates in a new UConn women’s basketball documentary set to be released on Apple TV.
articles.body:
Dallas Wings stars Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd are publicly discussing their romantic relationship for the first time since becoming WNBA teammates in a new UConn women’s basketball documentary set to be released on Apple TV.

The two have always chosen to keep their relationship private, not because they wanted to hide it, but because they did not want it to define their professional careers or influence the decisions they make in the WNBA.

This small glimpse has caught fans by surprise, as many had already accepted that the pair would continue keeping their relationship out of the spotlight.

Now, however, the moment has given fans hope that they could learn a little more about the relationship between the two WNBA stars.

Fudd and Bueckers have also asked reporters to respect their privacy regarding their relationship throughout Fudd’s rookie WNBA season.

articles.title: 'Not gonna dim my light': Fever's Sophie Cunningham doubles down on trans athlete stance
articles.standfirst: Cunningham’s latest comments show the controversy surrounding her isn’t going away anytime soon
articles.summary: Cunningham’s latest comments show the controversy surrounding her isn’t going away anytime soon
articles.body:
Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham has made it clear once again that she won’t back away from her controversial views on transgender athletes, despite previously suggesting she wanted to move beyond the debate and concentrate on basketball.

Cunningham told USA Today that she doesn’t believe players or fans should be censored at WNBA games for expressing their opinions. She specifically pointed to supporters wearing “trans kids belong” shirts, arguing that the messages weren’t violent or threatening.

“None of these shirts are violent or mean,” said Cunningham . “They express [a] belief. We may not agree, and that's fine.

“I think everybody should get to wear what they want, and I think the league is making a mistake by attempting to censor anybody.”

She also challenged league leadership to take a stronger approach to the ongoing controversy, suggesting that major decisions could ultimately rest with NBA commissioner Adam Silver.

The dispute dates back to a July ESPN interview in which Cunningham rejected the “MAGA Barbie” label and explained her concerns about transgender women competing in women’s sports. She said she wanted to protect young girls in locker rooms and athletic competition from having to face what she called “biological men.”

Her comments quickly became one of the WNBA’s biggest off-court talking points, prompting criticism from players, coaches and fans while also attracting vocal support from people who share her position.

Cunningham refuses to dim her light

The controversy has also followed Cunningham into arenas. She was booed by sections of the crowd during recent Fever road games, while supporters and opponents have staged demonstrations outside venues.

Fans have brought transgender pride flags and signs supporting trans athletes, while others have displayed messages backing Cunningham .

Cunningham , however, has repeatedly insisted that the attention hasn’t changed her approach. Earlier this month, she said she wanted to get back to basketball after describing the surrounding debate as a distraction.

She previously addressed rallies organized in support of her, saying she hadn’t been involved in arranging them and viewed the demonstrations as an example of people exercising their freedom of speech.

She also argued that the WNBA had an opportunity to demonstrate its commitment to diversity and inclusion by allowing different viewpoints to be expressed.

Cunningham’s message has remained consistent, as she’s stated she intends to play basketball while also standing behind her personal beliefs.

“I’m here to play basketball, but I’m also here to be me,” Cunningham said earlier this month. She added that she wasn’t going to hide or “dim my light” simply because some people disagreed with her.

That position has made Cunningham a polarizing figure, but she doesn’t appear interested in retreating from the spotlight. As criticism and support continue to surround her, the Fever guard is standing firmly behind her views while attempting to keep her attention on the court.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark gets star treatment in Canada as young fan surprises her before Toronto debut
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark has become accustomed to drawing enormous crowds throughout her WNBA career, but even the Indiana Fever superstar was surprised by the reception she received before her first professional game in Canada.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark has become accustomed to drawing enormous crowds throughout her WNBA career, but even the Indiana Fever superstar was surprised by the reception she received before her first professional game in Canada.

Clark’s arrival was one of the most anticipated moments of Toronto’s inaugural season. The Fever star was welcomed with plenty of excitement, but one young fan in particular stole the spotlight.

Before the game, a little girl presented Clark with a bouquet of flowers that was almost bigger than she was.

The young fan was visibly thrilled to meet the superstar after Clark signed her jersey and posed for photos with her, creating a memorable moment ahead of Clark’s first WNBA game in Canada.

articles.title: Enes Kanter encourages NBA players to enter the 2027 WNBA draft to secure better salaries
articles.standfirst: The former NBA center says the massive pay gap could motivate more players to test the league's eligibility rules
articles.summary: The former NBA center says the massive pay gap could motivate more players to test the league's eligibility rules
articles.body:
Former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom is escalating his challenge to the WNBA by claiming that more male basketball players could declare for the 2027 WNBA Draft if the league doesn't clarify its eligibility rules.

In a video posted Tuesday, Kanter said he'd spoken with eight players who were considering joining his campaign.

According to the former Boston Celtics player, the group includes two former NBA players, three G League players and three European players. None of those players has been publicly identified or independently confirmed Kanter's claim.

Kanter's argument centers heavily on the financial difference between the two leagues.

“Hear me out, the NBA G League pays players $45,000 a year, while the WNBA’s top players earn $1.4 million. Those ‘men’ could earn an extra $1,355,000 a year by just identifying as women. Rules are rules,” said Kanter .

The WNBA's new collective bargaining agreement has dramatically increased compensation. The league says its 2026 maximum salary is $1.4 million, while the average salary is projected to exceed $583,000. The agreement also runs through 2032 and introduces substantial salary growth across the league.

Kanter's campaign puts pressure on WNBA

Kanter first announced his intention to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft earlier this month, arguing that the league's collective bargaining agreement doesn't specifically define biological sex or gender identity beyond stating that women are eligible. Former NBA player Royce White subsequently made a similar declaration.

The controversy gained momentum after Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham publicly discussed transgender participation in women's sports. Her comments triggered a wider debate among players, supporters and critics.

The WNBA has since pushed back against the campaign. Its anti-hate task force said there are currently no immediate eligibility issues involving transgender athletes and condemned what it described as “bad-faith” attempts to demean or marginalize others.

The league also said discussions about the subject would continue with the players' association.

Kanter's latest comments appear designed to increase pressure on the league by suggesting that his challenge could become larger than a two-player protest. His claim that eight additional players are considering the move, however, remains unverified, and he hasn't named the individuals involved.

The former NBA big man has also framed the dispute as more than a question of eligibility. By highlighting the enormous difference between G League and WNBA compensation, he's attempting to present the proposed declarations as a financial opportunity as well as a political statement.

Whether any other players ultimately follow Kanter and White remains uncertain. The WNBA could also revise or clarify its eligibility standards before the 2027 draft, potentially changing the circumstances surrounding the campaign.

Kanter's recruiting pitch has added another layer to an already contentious debate. What began with questions surrounding transgender participation in women's basketball has expanded into a broader confrontation over league rules and how those policies should be interpreted.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd break their silence on relationship in new UConn documentary
articles.standfirst: A new glimpse has fans wondering how much more the documentary will reveal
articles.summary: A new glimpse has fans wondering how much more the documentary will reveal
articles.body:
At the start of the season, Paige Bueckers made it clear that Azzi Fudd’s arrival in Dallas had nothing to do with her. Fudd’s selection by the Dallas Wings was the result of her own work and everything she accomplished during her time with the UConn Huskies. Being the first pick in the WNBA Draft was not about their relationship , but about what Fudd had earned and what Dallas saw in her as a player.

For that same reason, the two players made it clear that their relationship would remain private and away from the media . They asked reporters to leave their relationship out of their coverage and focus entirely on basketball.

A trailer gave fans a glimpse they were not expecting

UConn fans are getting a new behind-the-scenes look at Geno Auriemma and his program through Apple TV’s new documentary series, T he Dynasty: UConn Huskies . The three-part series shows how Auriemma turned UConn into the most successful program in college basketball .

The trailer also includes Bueckers and Fudd publicly discussing their romantic relationship for the first time since becoming WNBA teammates. While some of what they shared had already been assumed by fans, seeing the two address their relationship in the documentary was enough to get fans excited about what else could be revealed .

Fans may finally get a closer look at the story

The small glimpse caught fans by surprise , especially after many had accepted that Bueckers and Fudd would continue keeping their relationship out of the spotlight . Now, the moment has given them hope that they could learn a little more about the relationship between the two WNBA stars.

Fudd and Bueckers have continued to ask reporters for privacy about their relationship during Fudd’s rookie WNBA season, keeping the focus on their careers while they adjust to being teammates with the Dallas Wings.

articles.title: WNBA fans blast Caitlin Clark's anthem posture while labeling Sophie Cunningham a 'true patriot'
articles.standfirst: Fans rally behind Sophie Cunningham while turning their criticism toward Caitlin Clark
articles.summary: Fans rally behind Sophie Cunningham while turning their criticism toward Caitlin Clark
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark has found herself at the center of another heated WNBA debate after footage from the national anthem prompted criticism from fans on social media.

The controversy unfolded before the Indiana Fever's game against the Atlanta Dream, when video appeared to show Sophie Cunningham standing with her right hand over her heart while Clark stood behind her with both hands behind her back.

Clark was facing the American flag and standing during the anthem, but her posture quickly became a talking point online. Some fans accused the Fever superstar of showing insufficient respect, while Cunningham was praised as a “true patriot” for making the hand-over-heart gesture.

One social media user described Cunningham as the only player demonstrating patriotism and criticized the other Fever players for not following the same gesture. Others went even further, directing personal criticism at Clark and arguing that athletes should always place their hands over their hearts during the national anthem.

“ Sophie Cunningham is the only good thing about the WNBA. Will support her but done with everything else,” wrote one fan.

However, not everyone agreed with that assessment. Some fans defended Clark and her teammates, pointing out that standing respectfully and facing the flag has traditionally been considered appropriate behavior. Others argued that the hand-over-heart gesture isn't necessarily the only way to demonstrate respect.

“The hand over the heart is a newer phenomenon and can sometimes be perceived as performative. Prior to the Trump year's, standing up straight in a respectful manner with your hat off worked just fine,” wrote one fan.

Anthem controversy adds to growing attention around Fever stars

The debate comes as both Clark and Cunningham continue to attract enormous attention away from the basketball court.

Clark delivered a major performance against Atlanta, scoring 26 points as Indiana secured a dramatic 95-91 overtime victory. Her performance was another reminder that the second-year superstar remains one of the biggest attractions in women's basketball.

The attention followed Clark to Toronto, where the Fever recently made their Canadian debut against the Toronto Tempo. The visiting star received an enthusiastic reception from supporters before putting together another impressive performance.

Clark scored 24 points, handed out seven assists and grabbed three rebounds as Indiana defeated Toronto 101-95. The game was played at Scotiabank Arena after the Tempo moved the contest from Coca-Cola Coliseum to accommodate the expected demand to see Clark in person.

While Clark was warmly welcomed, Cunningham received a much different reaction from sections of the Toronto crowd. The Fever forward has become a divisive figure following comments she made about transgender participation in women's sports.

Cunningham has insisted that she doesn't hate transgender people and has said her position comes from wanting to protect opportunities for biological females in women's athletics. Her comments have nevertheless generated significant criticism and support.

That backdrop helps explain why the anthem footage generated such an intense response. Cunningham already has a highly visible group of supporters, while Clark's enormous profile means even relatively routine pregame moments can quickly become viral talking points.

Regardless of where fans stand, the incident shows once again that Fever players are being scrutinized far beyond their performances on the court.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark feels the love from the opposition as young fan surprises her before Toronto debut
articles.standfirst: Clark may have arrived as the opponent, but Canada made sure she felt at home
articles.summary: Clark may have arrived as the opponent, but Canada made sure she felt at home
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark was surprised by the amount of love she received from fans in Canada despite stepping onto Canadian soil as the opposition . The Indiana Fever superstar has become accustomed to drawing enormous crowds throughout her WNBA career, but her first professional game in Canada gave her a different kind of welcome.

Clark’s arrival was one of the most anticipated moments of Toronto’s inaugural season. The Tempo joined the WNBA in 2026 as the league’s first Canadian franchise, giving local fans their first chance to watch Clark play a professional game on home soil.

A young fan made sure Clark’s Canadian debut came with a special memory

Before the game against the Toronto Tempo, a little girl handed Clark a bouquet of flowers that looked almost bigger than she was . The gesture quickly went viral, as the young fan got the chance to meet the superstar after Clark signed her jersey and posed for photos with her.

Whether Clark is a fan favorite or not, moments like this show what the WNBA can represent beyond teams and colors . The league is also about inspiring young girls who want to follow the same path as the players they watch on the court.

For Clark, basketball was once again proof that the game can bring people together

Clark was especially appreciative of the reception the Fever received in Canada . It was her first time visiting the country, and she left with a strong impression of the experience . She was happy to take in the culture and explore the city while seeing the excitement surrounding women’s basketball firsthand.

The Fever star thanked the fans for their support and said she had a lot of fun being in Canada . For Clark and her teammates, t he reception was a special reminder of how much the sport continues to connect people beyond the court.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers receives tough news after Azzi Fudd is ruled out for the rest of the season
articles.standfirst: Fudd was the first overall pick in the draft and played in 30 games this season
articles.summary: Fudd was the first overall pick in the draft and played in 30 games this season
articles.body:
The Dallas Wings are currently confronting hard questions about whether passing on Olivia Miles with the top selection in this year's draft was a mistake, especially given that Miles is not only a lock for Rookie of the Year but also firmly entrenched in the MVP conversation alongside A'ja Wilson and Caitlin Clark .

The Wings opted to take Azzi Fudd first overall. While Fudd is a remarkably gifted player, the selection was heavily influenced by her chemistry with Paige Bueckers , the number one pick and Rookie of the Year last season, with whom she captured a National Championship at UConn in 2025 and shares a close personal bond dating back to their college days.

Azzi Fudd Ruled Out for the Season

The decision not to draft Miles looks even more difficult now, as the franchise announced that Azzi Fudd will miss the rest of the season after undergoing arthroscopic surgery on her right knee.

The procedure, designed to address persistent soreness in the joint, is scheduled for early next week in Connecticut. The UConn product first experienced right knee discomfort during warmups prior to the Wings' game against the Golden State Valkyries on August 7.

Although Dallas initially held her out of that matchup out of an abundance of caution, she missed the subsequent five games before the team officially confirmed the season-ending procedure.

During an impressive debut campaign, Fudd appeared in 30 games, averaging 13.1 points, 1.8 assists, 1.7 rebounds, and 1.7 steals (ranking fifth-best in the league in steals).

A Familiar Injury Battle and a Major Blow to Dallas' Playoff Push

With Fudd sidelined for the duration, this marks the first time since 2021 that the first overall pick will not capture the Rookie of the Year award, following a run by Rhyne Howard , Aliyah Boston , Caitlin Clark , and Paige Bueckers over the past four seasons.

For the Wings, the absolute priority is ensuring Fudd makes a full recovery for the future, as the 23-year-old remains a cornerstone of the franchise alongside Bueckers.

Unfortunately, knee injuries have repeatedly interrupted her career path: she previously tore her right ACL and medial meniscus during college, causing her to miss the bulk of the 2023-24 season, and also suffered severe ACL and MCL tears in her right knee back in April 2019.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese prove their value as their latest matchup becomes the WNBA's most-watched game of the season
articles.standfirst: The game was the most-viewed WNBA game in ESPN's network history
articles.summary: The game was the most-viewed WNBA game in ESPN's network history
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever are on a five-game winning streak and sit third in the WNBA standings , with three of their last four victories coming in dominant fashion against the Liberty , Wings , and an overtime thriller against the Dream , all teams expected to be major factors in the playoffs.

The biggest catalyst behind the Fever's soaring success is their high-octane offense, averaging 96.4 points per game , the most ever in WNBA history , led by Kelsey Mitchell ( 24.3 PPG ) and Caitlin Clark ( 22.1 PPG ), who rank second and third in points per game this season.

So far, each star has scored 20+ points in the same game 16 times this season, establishing a new WNBA single-season record for a duo .

Mitchell is currently riding a blistering streak of 20 consecutive games scoring 20+ points , while Clark, combining her scoring output with a league-leading 8.3 assists per game , is authoring the most offensively productive season the WNBA has ever witnessed.

Clark and Reese Shatter WNBA Viewership Records

The Fever don't just dominate on the hardwood; they command television screens nationwide, owning the five most-watched games of the season.

Their latest 95-91 overtime win over the Atlanta Dream and Angel Reese is now officially the most-watched WNBA game on cable in the league's 30-season history , per WNBA Communications, averaging 2.6 million viewers and peaking at 4 million .

Since Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese arrived in the league in 2024, the WNBA has experienced exponential growth in viewership.

While Clark remains the primary driving force, with the Fever starring in the most-watched broadcasts overall, the highest-rated regular-season games consistently feature matchups against Reese.

A postseason series between Clark and Reese would be the ultimate gift for basketball fans, though regardless of who Indiana faces, any Fever playoff series is guaranteed to draw record crowds because Clark's historic offensive style is unlike anything the WNBA has ever seen.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham has a dream business partner, but her big plan sounds more like a vacation
articles.standfirst: Her dream venture sounds more like a permanent vacation
articles.summary: Her dream venture sounds more like a permanent vacation
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham already seems to be thinking about life beyond basketball, but her dream business might not involve much actual work. The Indiana Fever star was asked which WNBA player she would choose as a business partner, and she needed little time to settle on one very famous former teammate.

Cunningham picked WNBA legend Diana Taurasi, whom she played alongside for six seasons with the Phoenix Mercury. Her reason, however, quickly turned the hypothetical business pitch into something closer to the ultimate vacation plan.

“I’d probably go Diana Taurasi because she has the finances,” Cunningham joked during an interview with Front Office Sports. She then imagined their “business” taking place on a yacht or boat, somewhere on a lake or the ocean, with drinks flowing and plenty of time to work on a tan all, importantly, on Taurasi’s budget.

The answer was clearly playful, but Cunningham knew exactly whom she was choosing. Taurasi spent 20 seasons in the WNBA and also enjoyed an enormously successful international career, including lucrative years playing overseas, making her joke about the basketball icon having the money to fund their luxurious venture even better.

Cunningham, meanwhile, is building an increasingly valuable profile of her own. Her popularity has exploded away from the court, opening opportunities in endorsements, media and potentially other ventures that could become even more important whenever her playing career comes to an end.

So perhaps Cunningham really does have the beginnings of a post-WNBA business plan. There is just one question left after hearing the details: does she actually want to start a company with Diana Taurasi or simply make sure she is always on vacation with her?

articles.title: Does Sophie Cunningham have a sister? This story explains a lot about the WNBA star
articles.standfirst: Sophie was not the first player in her family to stand out. Before her came Lindsey, her older sister, with whom she shared a court and a passion that began long before reaching college.
articles.summary: Sophie was not the first player in her family to stand out. Before her came Lindsey, her older sister, with whom she shared a court and a passion that began long before reaching college.
articles.body:
Long before making it to the WNBA, Sophie Cunningham had a rival very close to home. Her older sister, Lindse y, also played basketball and ended up becoming one of the most important people in her development.

The WNBA star is now one of the recognizable faces of American women’s basketball; however, there was one key person in her life who was there long before the spotlight appeared: Lindsey, her older sister.

Sophie's first rival was at home

Sophie Cunningham didn’t reach elite basketball alone. Before becoming one of the most recognized figures in Missouri women’s basketball and later making the jump to the WNBA, she had a fundamental role model at home: her older sister, Lindsey Cunningham Hudson.

They both grew up in Columbia, Missouri, in a family deeply connected to sports and the University of Missouri . Mizzou itself identifies Lindsey as Sophie’s older sister and notes that both played basketball for the Tigers . They are the daughters of Jim and Paula Cunningham , two former Mizzou athletes. Jim played football for the Tigers , while Paula competed in track and field. The family’s sporting tradition went even beyond their parents: other members of the Cunningham family also had athletic ties to Missouri.

Sophie grew up in an environment where sports were part of everyday life, something that helped fuel her enormous competitiveness from a very young age. She and her sister, who is two years older, especially stood out in basketball and soccer.

The two sisters ended up sharing a locker room on the University of Missouri team. When Sophie arrived in 2015, Lindsey was already in the program, and they overlapped for two seasons, 2015–2016.

Lindsey played 129 games during her college career and in her final season she was an important part of the team, serving as captain, while Sophie was beginning to build a career that would end up making her one of the greatest players in the program's history.

For Sophie , however, her sister's numbers were almost secondary. What mattered was that Lindsey had already traveled the path she wanted to follow. She watched her train, compete, and face situations that she too would later have to face.

The present day of Lindsey Cunningham

The older sister of the current WNBA star retired from competitive basketball after finishing her college career. She then remained involved in the sport in other areas, including coaching, although she would later distance herself completely from the activity.

Her path ended up being different from Sophie's, who kept moving forward until she reached the highest level of women's basketball in the world, the WNBA . However, the connection with Missouri remained an important part of her sports story.

Today Sophie is the one taking center stage and competing in the WNBA, while Lindsey chose to step away from professional basketball. However, before the big games arrived and the spotlight shone on the younger of the Cunningham sisters, there was an older sister who had already shown her what it was like to chase the same dream.

articles.title: "Disrespectful Stunt": Ex-NBA stars under fire after Caitlin Clark claim and brutal Angel Reese warning
articles.standfirst: Patrick Beverley has condemned Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White over WNBA 2027 draft declarations
articles.summary: Patrick Beverley has condemned Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White over WNBA 2027 draft declarations
articles.body:
What began as another argument over transgender participation in women’s sports has now pulled several former NBA players into a fight over the WNBA , and Patrick Beverley believes the conversation has gone badly off course.

Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White have both said they intend to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft as a challenge to the league’s eligibility rules. Their declarations followed renewed debate around the issue, including comments from Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham .

Beverley , who has frequently spoken positively about women’s basketball, has little patience for the way the two former players are making their point.

“Enes Kanter, Royce White, I don't like what y'all are doing at all,” Beverley said on The Pat Bev Show. “I think y'all disrespecting the brand that showed y'all a lot of respect. I think y'all disrespecting the game of basketball, period.”

His criticism was particularly pointed toward Kanter Freedom , who spent more than a decade in the NBA.

“You've made a name for being in the NBA, and you gonna come in here and say you want to try out for the WNBA?” Beverley added. “I understand the point y'all are trying to make. What y'all doing, it ain't right.”

Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese pulled into campaign

Kanter Freedom has made some of the loudest comments surrounding the planned draft effort. He recently said he would like to join Caitlin Clark with the Indiana Fever , imagining the pair as a new version of Kobe Bryant and Shaquille O'Neal .

“Think about this… We're going down the lane, Caitlin throws me a lob and I cut the lob and dunk the ball,” Kanter Freedom said. “Then me and Caitlin bump chests… which I'm allowed to do now, because I'm a woman.”

He later turned his attention toward Angel Reese , writing on X: “Sis! Once I go No.1 pick in the 2027 @WNBA Draft, the first player I'm dunking on is Angel Reese.”

The WNBA collective bargaining agreement says only women are eligible to play, while the supplied material notes that the language doesn't set out a more detailed definition there.

The league has characterized the former players’ campaign as a “bad-faith” effort.

Message does not justify the method

Beverley didn't spend his criticism debating the underlying policy. His objection centered on using the league and its players as the vehicle for a stunt.

“Regardless of what message y'all trying to get out there, bro, there's a way to do it,” Beverley said. “It's a hundred ways to skin a cat.”

Kanter Freedom has rejected the suggestion that he is trying to ridicule the WNBA.

“I'm not here to mock, make fun of, or disrespect any group or personal decisions,” he said. “I don't want this whole thing to turn into a laughing stock. I want people to take our message seriously.”

That defense hasn't changed Beverley ’s view. The 2027 WNBA draft remains months away, but the controversy has already become bigger than any realistic basketball outcome.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham blatantly hints WNBA chief Cathy Engelbert could get the boot
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever guard has questioned whether the WNBA commissioner’s job could be open after the season
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever guard has questioned whether the WNBA commissioner’s job could be open after the season
articles.body:
The WNBA has rarely had more momentum, but the relationship between its players and league leadership is becoming harder to ignore.

Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham has added to that tension by suggesting commissioner Cathy Engelbert ’s job could be in play at the end of the season, arguing that the league needs leadership willing to match the ambition of the players driving its growth.

“You do have to have a person in power who is bold, who is confident, who wants the best for the players and not maybe for themselves all the time,” Cunningham told USA Today.

“So I do feel like, as a whole, that could be a position that's maybe open at the end of the year, but that's not my call.”

The remarks are significant because Cunningham didn't dismiss Engelbert ’s record altogether. Instead, she framed the issue around whether the commissioner remains the right person for a league entering another pivotal period.

WNBA players can see much bigger league

Engelbert has led the WNBA since 2019 and has overseen a period of major commercial and audience growth.

Even so, Cunningham suggested that players believe there is still another level available if league leadership is willing to push aggressively enough.

“[Engelbert's] done a lot of good things, but with where our league is trying to go, I feel like you just want someone who also wants that,” Cunningham said.

“That's just a hard position to be in, in her shoes, us as players, we always want more, more, more because we see how good it can be, but that's up to [NBA commissioner] Adam Silver at the end of the day.”

The Fever guard has criticized Engelbert before. During an October 2025 episode of her podcast, she objected to the way the commissioner spoke about the league's rise.

“There's millions and millions of new fans, and at the end of the day, she's worried about her,” Cunningham said. “Cathy, no one cares. Literally, no one cares.”

Engelbert facing pressure from multiple directions

Minnesota Lynx star Napheesa Collier has also publicly challenged the league office over player welfare and labor issues, increasing scrutiny on management as another major round of collective bargaining approaches.

Cunningham , meanwhile, has become one of the league's most polarizing figures after speaking about transgender participation in women's sports.

“I got a lot of negative feedback about me hating trans. And I'm like, ‘I never once said that,’” Cunningham told ESPN. “I think that I am here to extend love. But I also think with that love is truth, being honest.”

Her comments triggered protests and wider political attention, while the league subsequently called for thoughtful discussion and rejected what it characterized as “bad-faith” arguments around eligibility.

That controversy has now become part of a much broader leadership debate. The question surrounding Engelbert is no longer whether the WNBA has grown under her watch.

It's whether the players at the center of that growth believe she is still the person they want leading what comes next.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and the big stars already preparing for the FIBA World Cup: it all begins on September 4
articles.standfirst: Berlin prepares for the FIBA World Cup: Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese and a list of big stars.
articles.summary: Berlin prepares for the FIBA World Cup: Caitlin Clark, Angel Reese and a list of big stars.
articles.body:
The FIBA 2026 Women's Basketball World Cup will bring together the best and most prestigious players on the planet. The leading stars of each national team will seek to lead their squads to the title.

The tournament will be held in Berlin, Germany . From September 4 to 13, the best national teams in the world will meet in the German capital to compete for the world title.

Among the names drawing the most attention are Caitlin Clark, A’ja Wilson and Angel Reese , three of the most recognizable figures in American basketball. But they will not be the only stars in the spotlight.

Completing a roster loaded with stars are Breanna Stewart, Paige Bueckers, Kelsey Plum and Napheesa Collier , rounding out a U.S. lineup packed with WNBA stars. Stewart arrives as one of the team’s main leaders and a player who already knows what it means to be a world champion; Bueckers , meanwhile, is expected to play in her first senior World Cup with the United States. Plum and Collier are also part of a generation that combines experience and talent at the highest professional level.

It should be noted that FIBA has indicated that the U.S. list includes 12 players, although it does not necessarily yet represent the final roster that will compete in the tournament.

The United States will not be the only national team with big names: Spain, Australia, Belgium, France, Japan, Germany, Italy, China, Turkey and the rest of the 16 participants complete a World Cup that will feature representation from four continents.

In addition to the players already included, there are also, for example, Ezi Magbegor and Sami Whitcomb with Australia, Emma Meesseman and Julie Vanloo with Belgium, and Alba Torrens and María Conde with Spain.

The tournament will be divided into four groups. Spain, Japan, Germany, and Mali make up Group A; France, Hungary, Korea, and Nigeria will be in Group B; Belgium, Australia, Puerto Rico, and Turkey will play in Group C; while the United States, Italy, China, and the Czech Republic were placed in Group D.

With the World Cup expanded from 12 to 16 teams, Berlin is preparing to host an even more open competition with an unprecedented number of stars.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers face off again six days after neither could outscore the other
articles.standfirst: Their last scoring battle ended even, but Indiana won
articles.summary: Their last scoring battle ended even, but Indiana won
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark scored 29 points. Paige Bueckers scored 29 points. For an entire night, two of the biggest names in the WNBA kept answering each other, and when their individual scoring battle was finally over, neither had managed to put one more point on the board than the other. There was only one difference that really mattered: Clark's Indiana Fever walked away with the 98-87 victory. Six days later, they get to do it all over again .

Clark and the Fever arrive in Dallas on Thursday at 24-12 and riding five consecutive victories, while Bueckers and the Wings are 20-16 and trying to stop a much more uncomfortable stretch after losing seven of their last 10. This is also the final regular-season meeting between the teams, giving Dallas one last opportunity to respond after what happened in Indianapolis less than a week ago.

Face to face again, who wins?

And those 29 points don't tell the whole story of their first duel. Clark scored 16 in the third quarter alone and finished with 10 assists, while Bueckers added six rebounds and six assists to her 29 points.

Every time one appeared ready to take control, the other seemed capable of answering. But Indiana had something Dallas couldn't match that night: more help around its star. Kelsey Mitchell added 23 points, giving Clark and Mitchell 52 between them and helping turn an individual draw into a Fever victory.

That difference could become even more important Thursday because Bueckers will again be without Azzi Fudd. The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft will miss the remainder of her rookie season and undergo arthroscopic surgery on her right knee after persistent soreness.

Fudd was averaging 13.1 points and had become one of Dallas' most dangerous perimeter weapons, leading all rookies in made three-pointers. The Wings are just 1-4 since she was sidelined, leaving even more responsibility on Bueckers as Dallas fights to hold onto a playoff position.

Indiana has the opposite feeling right now. Clark is creating, Mitchell keeps scoring and the Fever are winning. Mitchell enters the night averaging 24.3 points per game, while Clark is producing 8.3 assists, and together they give Indiana two different problems for a defense to solve: concentrate too much on Clark and Mitchell can punish you; focus on stopping Mitchell and Clark can begin finding everyone else.

And then there is Sophie Cunningham. She may not carry the same scoring expectations as Clark, Bueckers or Mitchell , but few players arrive in Dallas surrounded by as much attention.

Cunningham has become one of the most talked-about personalities in the league, and that adds another unpredictable element to a game already filled with them. Maybe Mitchell takes over.

Maybe Bueckers responds without Fudd. Maybe Cunningham produces the moment everyone talks about afterward. Or perhaps Clark and Bueckers simply pick up where they left off six days ago.

This is also the final regular-season meeting between the teams, giving Dallas one last opportunity to respond after what happened in Indianapolis less than a week ago.
Face to face again, who wins?

And those 29 points don't tell the whole story of their first duel. Clark scored 16 in the third quarter alone and finished with 10 assists, while Bueckers added six rebounds and six assists to her 29 points.

Every time one appeared ready to take control, the other seemed capable of answering. But Indiana had something Dallas couldn't match that night: more help around its star. Kelsey Mitchell added 23 points, giving Clark and Mitchell 52 between them and helping turn an individual draw into a Fever victory.

That difference could become even more important Thursday because Bueckers will again be without Azzi Fudd. The No. 1 overall pick in the 2026 WNBA Draft will miss the remainder of her rookie season and undergo arthroscopic surgery on her right knee after persistent soreness.

Fudd was averaging 13.1 points and had become one of Dallas' most dangerous perimeter weapons, leading all rookies in made three-pointers. The Wings are just 1-4 since she was sidelined, leaving even more responsibility on Bueckers as Dallas fights to hold onto a playoff position.

Indiana has the opposite feeling right now. Clark is creating, Mitchell keeps scoring and the Fever are winning. Mitchell enters the night averaging 24.3 points per game, while Clark is producing 8.3 assists, and together they give Indiana two different problems for a defense to solve: concentrate too much on Clark and Mitchell can punish you; focus on stopping Mitchell and Clark can begin finding everyone else.
And then there is Sophie Cunningham. She may not carry the same scoring expectations as Clark, Bueckers or Mitchell , but few players arrive in Dallas surrounded by as much attention.
Cunningham has become one of the most talked-about personalities in the league, and that adds another unpredictable element to a game already filled with them. Maybe Mitchell takes over.
Maybe Bueckers responds without Fudd. Maybe Cunningham produces the moment everyone talks about afterward. Or perhaps Clark and Bueckers simply pick up where they left off six days ago.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers tells Caitlin Clark to “Calm Down” while everyone says they hate each other
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers’ rivalry reached a fiery moment after a heated exchange during the Fever-Wings matchup.
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and Paige Bueckers’ rivalry reached a fiery moment after a heated exchange during the Fever-Wings matchup.
articles.body:
The play occurred in the final seconds of the second quarter. With less than 10 seconds remaining, Clark had possession and the Wings had a foul to give in order to stop the clock. Bueckers , who was defending Indiana’s star, decided to grab her left arm to commit the foul.

Caitlin Clark clearly did not take the action well. While Paige Bueckers maintained contact to ensure the foul was called, the Fever guard reacted angrily and then threw the ball toward the other end of the court, passing close to the Dallas player’s head.

Clark’s frustration continued for several seconds until Bueckers gestured for her to “calm down.” Ultimately, the incident resulted in a personal foul on the Wings guard and did not escalate further.

However, the moment quickly sparked discussion among women’s basketball fans , as it involved two of the biggest stars of the WNBA’s new generation.

Despite the exchange, both players have maintained a mutual respect. Their rivalry dates back to their college days, when they were already considered two of the sport’s top young prospects.

Caitlin Clark had previously praised Paige Bueckers

The Fever and Wings had faced each other just days earlier, on August 14 , in a matchup where both stars shined: Clark and Bueckers each scored 29 points in Indiana’s 98-87 victory.

After that game, Clark praised her opponent’s talent and acknowledged how difficult she is to defend.

“Obviously, she’s an incredible player. She makes it really hard on us defensively... Paige is a tremendous player. She takes what the defense gives her; she doesn’t force anything; she’s smooth; she finds the open teammate. So she’s just a really tough guard.”

Both stars are expected to be asked about the incident, although everything points to it being a product of the intensity of the game. Additionally, they will share the United States jersey at next month’s FIBA World Cup , where they can channel that competitive fire into a strength as teammates.

articles.title: How the Dallas Wings ended Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever’s winning streak
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark was silenced, and the Fever’s winning streak came crashing down against Dallas.
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark was silenced, and the Fever’s winning streak came crashing down against Dallas.
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever saw their five-game winning streak come to an end after falling to the Dallas Wings in a game where their top players were unable to find their best offensive form.

Indiana got off to a strong start, but the momentum quickly shifted. Caitlin Clark had one of her quietest offensive nights of the season, finishing with just 10 points after shooting 4-of-15 from the field . The Fever guard made up for it somewhat with 9 assists , but she was unable to establish her usual rhythm.

On the other side, Paige Bueckers also failed to replicate the standout performance she delivered in the previous matchup between the two teams. The two young stars had a disappointing showdown, with Bueckers finishing with 13 points on just 5-of-16 shooting .

The lone exception for Indiana was Kelsey Mitchell , who continued her incredible scoring run. The guard surpassed 20 points for the 21st consecutive game , setting a new WNBA record for consecutive games reaching that mark. Mitchell finished the night with 37 points .

However, Dallas found answers from multiple players. Jessica Shepard delivered a historic performance with 26 points, a career high, carrying the Wings’ offense in the first half. Then Arike Ogunbowale took over in the second half, finishing the game with 32 points.

Meanwhile, Awak Kuier took advantage of her opportunity as a starter with Azzi Fudd sidelined due to injury. The Dallas forward made a major impact defensively, recording 11 points, 8 rebounds, and 7 blocks , consistently disrupting Indiana’s drives to the basket.

The Fever also struggled on the boards. Dallas won the rebounding battle 32-28 , a difference that proved crucial in the final outcome.

Fever continue a challenging road trip

The loss came during one of the toughest stretches of Indiana’s schedule. It was the t hird road game of a five-game trip in just eight days .

Before visiting Dallas , the Fever picked up important wins in Atlanta and Toronto , but they now must quickly regroup. Indiana will face the New York Liberty in Brooklyn on Saturday before finishing the trip against the Chicago Sky on Sunday.

While every victory matters in the race for playoff positioning and the chance to secure home-court advantage in the first round, keeping the team healthy throughout this demanding stretch is just as important.

After this road trip, Indiana will play one final home game against the Connecticut Sun on August 28 before the break for the FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup .

Caitlin Clark and Aliyah Boston will represent the United States in the tournament in Berlin, and the break could provide a valuable reset as both players share the court with a star-studded roster.

With the loss, the Fever dropped to 24-13 and remain in a tight battle with the Las Vegas Aces and the Atlanta Dream to determine the third through fifth seeds in the standings.

articles.title: Angel Reese makes WNBA history against the Sparks, and her reaction goes viral
articles.standfirst: The Dream star went 9-for-9 from the field and celebrated record-breaking first half
articles.summary: The Dream star went 9-for-9 from the field and celebrated record-breaking first half
articles.body:
There was no need for Angel Reese to answer any of her critics Thursday night. Her stat line did it for her.

The Atlanta Dream forward produced a flawless shooting performance in a 124-88 rout of the Los Angeles Sparks , finishing with 20 points, 10 rebounds, eight assists and three steals while going 9-for-9 from the field and 2-for-2 from beyond the arc.

Yet one of the most memorable moments came before the final buzzer.

After making WNBA history during the first half, Reese turned toward the crowd, covered her mouth and waved before posing with her back to the stands.

The Dream bench rose to celebrate with her as fans inside Crypto.com Arena responded enthusiastically.

By halftime, Reese had already gone 8-for-8 while recording at least 15 points, five rebounds and five assists, becoming the first player in WNBA history to reach those marks in a half without missing a shot.

Perfect shooting night and record-breaking performance

The history didn't stop there. According to ESPN Insights, Reese became only the third player in WNBA history to record a 20-point double-double while shooting 100% from the field.

She also became the first player in league history to finish a game with at least 20 points, 10 rebounds and five assists without missing a field goal.

“ANGEL REESE LEGACY GAME,” Real App posted during the performance.

Another post summed it up even more simply: “Angel Reese had a perfect game.” ESPN's Sam Block added: “Y'all can keep hating. She's gonna keep hooping.”

That reaction carried particular weight because Reese 's offensive efficiency has frequently been scrutinized. Seven of her nine baskets came from within three feet, while the other two came from beyond the 3-point line.

Reese breaks another record

Reese also collected her 173rd offensive rebound of the season, breaking the single-season WNBA record she had established with 172 during her rookie year with the Chicago Sky in 2024.

Before Reese , the mark belonged to Yolanda Griffith , who grabbed 162 offensive rebounds for the Sacramento Monarchs in 2001.

The milestone added to a season already packed with them. Reese became the fastest player in league history to reach 1,000 career rebounds, getting there in 79 games, and has also established a new Dream single-season rebounding record.

Atlanta's entire offense was nearly unstoppable against Los Angeles. The Dream shot 64% from the field and 62% from 3-point range, with Rhyne Howard scoring a game-high 26 points and Jordin Canada handing out 11 assists.

The Sparks , playing without Kelsey Plum , never recovered from a 34-12 first quarter and trailed by as many as 42. Atlanta is now firmly in the race for home-court advantage in the postseason.

Thursday, however, belonged to Reese . A perfect shooting night, multiple pieces of WNBA history and one celebratory reaction ensured everyone inside the building knew it.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers could pay the price after heated Caitlin Clark clash
articles.standfirst: The Dallas Wings star lost her cool after a call involving Clark and could now face a fine from the WNBA
articles.summary: The Dallas Wings star lost her cool after a call involving Clark and could now face a fine from the WNBA
articles.body:
P aige Bueckers' frustration boiled over during the Dallas Wings' matchup against Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever, and one heated reaction could now cost her.

The Dallas guard was assessed a technical foul after arguing with an official over a call involving Clark, putting Bueckers in line for a potential $500 fine under the WNBA's new rules.

The incident unfolded in the fourth quarter after Indiana forward Makayla Timpson grabbed a defensive rebound and sent the ball to Clark. As the Fever star pushed down the court, she found herself one-on-one against Bueckers.

Bueckers was called for a personal foul as Clark attempted to get past her, but the Wings star immediately disagreed with the decision. She appeared to believe Clark had pushed off and made her frustration clear to the official.

The argument went too far

Bueckers was hit with a technical foul after exchanging words with the referee, a decision that could now come with a financial consequence.

Under the WNBA's new CBA, players are fined $500 for each of their first three technical fouls. Technical fouls four through seven carry a $1,000 fine, while an eighth results in a $1,500 fine and an automatic one-game suspension.

Bueckers had previously been assessed a technical against the Atlanta Dream on May 22, but that call was later rescinded.

That makes the technical against Indiana particularly significant for the Wings guard, who could now have to pay for allowing her frustration to spill over.

Caitlin Clark has been walking an even thinner line

Clark knows better than most how quickly technical fouls can become costly.

The Fever star has been assessed eight technicals during the 2026 season, putting her at the center of the WNBA's disciplinary rules. However, her most recent technical against the Chicago Sky on August 8 was later rescinded, allowing her to avoid an automatic one-game suspension.

Dallas ultimately had the last word on the scoreboard, beating Indiana 91-85 and snapping the Fever's five-game winning streak. Arike Ogunbowale led the Wings with a game-high 32 points , while Bueckers finished with 13 points , eight assists and six rebounds. For Indiana, Aliyah Boston posted 19 points and nine rebounds, while Clark was held to 10 points on 4-of-15 shooting but still contributed nine assists.

For Bueckers, there is no suspension threat yet. But unless the league decides to rescind Thursday's technical as well, the confrontation could leave the Dallas star with a $500 reminder of what happened when her frustration against Clark boiled over.

articles.title: Angel Reese has hilarious NSFW reaction to sex toy thrown on WNBA court
articles.standfirst: A bizarre interruption gave Reese another unforgettable viral moment
articles.summary: A bizarre interruption gave Reese another unforgettable viral moment
articles.body:
Angel Reese had an unforgettable reaction to one of the strangest moments of the WNBA season during the Atlanta Dream’s 124-88 demolition of the Los Angeles Sparks on Thursday night.

With 2:59 remaining in the third quarter, a neon green sex toy was thrown onto the court as Sparks forward Jihyun Park prepared to shoot free throws. The object landed in front of Park before bouncing across the paint toward Los Angeles’ bench, briefly stopping the action.

Reese , who was sitting near the scorer’s table, appeared to immediately spot the person responsible. She jumped up and pointed toward the stands, repeatedly alerting those nearby and saying, “Right there! Get him!”

Video of the moment quickly went viral, with some lip-readers claiming Reese also made another NSFW comment about the size of the object. That portion of the exchange hasn’t been independently confirmed, but Reese’s animated reaction was certainly hard to miss.

Cameron Brink then kicked the object away before security removed it from the court. Reports indicated the alleged thrower was caught by arena security after Reese helped identify the person.

Reese turned a bizarre interruption into another memorable night

The bizarre incident also brought back memories of similar disruptions during the 2025 WNBA season. Sex toys were thrown onto the court during multiple games, including matchups involving the Dream, Golden State Valkyries and Chicago Sky.

The incidents eventually faded, but Thursday’s episode showed that the unusual trend hasn’t completely disappeared. However, the interruption was only a footnote in an outstanding individual performance for Reese .

The Atlanta star was perfect from the field, knocking down all nine of her attempts while making both of her three-point attempts. She finished with 20 points, 10 rebounds, eight assists and three steals, recording her 25th double-double of the season.

The performance also made her only the third player in WNBA history to post a 20-point double-double while shooting 100 percent from the floor.

Reese also made history on the offensive glass. Four offensive rebounds during the contest pushed her season total beyond the 172 she recorded in 2024, allowing her to break her own WNBA single-season record. She now has eight regular-season games left to extend the mark even further.

The Dream made history as well, scoring a franchise-record 124 points in the blowout. Rhyne Howard led Atlanta with 26 points, including five three-pointers, while the victory also officially eliminated the Sparks from playoff contention.

While the bizarre object briefly stole attention from the basketball, Reese made sure the lasting story from Los Angeles was her spectacular performance. Between a perfect shooting night, another record and a viral reaction from the bench, it was certainly a game she won't soon forget.

articles.title: “Joker would be the most athletic player in the WNBA”: Fans mock Lexie Brown for her comparison with Nikola Jokic
articles.standfirst: The former WNBA champion attempted to challenge criticism of women's basketball, but her Nikola Jokic comparison quickly became the focus of the debate
articles.summary: The former WNBA champion attempted to challenge criticism of women's basketball, but her Nikola Jokic comparison quickly became the focus of the debate
articles.body:
L exie Brown has reignited an ongoing conversation about the athleticism of WNBA players after using Denver Nuggets superstar Nikola Jokic as part of her response to Michael Porter Jr.' s criticism of the women's game.

Brown's wider argument was aimed at challenging the idea that basketball must involve constant above-the-rim action to be considered athletic or entertaining.

But one particular comment about Jokic prompted a very different reaction from fans, many of whom questioned her description of the three-time NBA MVP.

The debate stems from comments Porter Jr. previously made about the WNBA, in which he questioned aspects of the league's athleticism and entertainment value. The former Nuggets forward had also suggested that lowering the rim could make women's basketball more exciting.

Those remarks generated considerable backlash from WNBA players and supporters. Brown has now revisited the subject during an appearance with Porter Jr. on the Curious Mike YouTube channel, attempting to make the point that elite basketball does not always require spectacular dunks or explosive leaping.

Brown pointed toward Jokic , who spent years alongside Porter Jr. in Denver, as an example of an NBA superstar whose effectiveness does not depend on playing above the rim.

She said: “The point I made about, you know, you eating off a player that plays below the rim and isn’t really athletic and like it wasn’t a shot to you. And I told you that the other night, like I think you’re an amazing player. And I think that, you know, you’ve dealt with your hardships, your injuries and stuff.

“But for the comment of like, “Oh, they’re not athletic. They’re not exciting.” And I’m like, “You literally played with Jokic.” Like, I wouldn’t say he’s not exciting, but he’s a below the rim player. Like, he’s not very fundamental.”

Why fans pushed back on the Jokic comparison

Brown's central point, that athleticism can manifest itself in ways other than jumping, is difficult to dispute. Strength, balance, coordination, reaction speed, endurance and body control are all important components of basketball.

However, fans immediately focused on her claim that Jokic is “not very fundamental.”

That description was particularly controversial because Jokic's game is widely regarded as being built around technical precision rather than explosive athleticism.

His footwork, passing, positioning, touch and ability to manipulate defenders have made him one of the most difficult players in the NBA to defend.

The numbers underline just how unusual his all-around game has become. During the 2025-26 regular season, Jokic averaged 27.7 points, 12.9 rebounds and 10.7 assists while shooting 56.9% from the field and 38% from three-point range.

He also led the NBA in both rebounding and assists, according to Basketball-Reference.

That combination is precisely why many fans rejected the suggestion that Jokic lacks fundamentals. His success comes largely from his ability to read the floor several steps ahead, make difficult passes and consistently exploit defensive weaknesses.

The backlash also overshadowed the broader point Brown was trying to make.

WNBA players have repeatedly pushed back against comparisons that reduce athleticism to dunking. Women's basketball features different physical and tactical characteristics, but the absence of frequent above-the-rim plays does not mean players lack speed, strength, agility or endurance.

Brown herself has considerable experience from inside the league. The former Duke standout was selected ninth overall in the 2018 WNBA Draft and won a championship with the Chicago Sky in 2021 before later playing for the Los Angeles Sparks and Seattle Storm.

She has also previously defended the WNBA against Porter Jr.'s comments. In 2024, Brown responded to his discussion of the league by pointing out that he himself was not known primarily for high-flying basketball.

Her latest appearance therefore continues a conversation she has been involved in for several years.

Porter Jr. , meanwhile, has since addressed some of the controversy surrounding his earlier remarks, creating an opportunity for Brown to explain her position directly.

The exchange demonstrates why discussions about the WNBA's athleticism can become so contentious.

There is a legitimate conversation to be had about differences between the men's and women's games, but defining athletic ability purely through dunks or vertical explosiveness ignores many of the skills that make basketball difficult.

Ironically, Jokic may be the perfect example of that principle.

He is not celebrated because of his vertical leap. He dominates because of his extraordinary coordination, size, strength, touch, anticipation and basketball intelligence.

His career, including three MVP awards and the 2023 NBA championship, is evidence that elite athletic performance does not have to look the same for every player.

For Brown , that was ultimately the message she wanted to communicate.

But for many fans, the discussion became less about her defence of WNBA players and more about whether one of the NBA's greatest offensive minds could reasonably be described as lacking fundamentals.

And that distinction has ensured the debate over Brown's comments is likely to continue well beyond the original conversation.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham savvy with finances: How is the Indiana Fever star investing massive new $665,000 contract?
articles.standfirst: The WNBA veteran is turning her career earnings into a growing real-estate portfolio
articles.summary: The WNBA veteran is turning her career earnings into a growing real-estate portfolio
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham is taking a notably different approach to the increased earnings available to WNBA players in 2026.

Rather than treating her new salary as an opportunity for extravagant spending, the Indiana Fever guard is using the money to build a business outside basketball.

Cunningham signed a one-year contract worth $665,000 to remain with the Fever after entering free agency during the offseason.

The deal represents a major financial leap for the 30-year-old, whose combined WNBA contract earnings across her first seven seasons were reportedly $569,022, according to Spotrac.

That comparison puts the significance of the new agreement into perspective. Cunningham is set to earn more in one season than she did across her first seven years in the league.

The dramatic increase is part of a broader shift in WNBA compensation following the league's new collective bargaining agreement.

The agreement has created a much different financial environment for players, particularly established veterans who have spent years earning comparatively modest salaries.

For Cunningham , however, the extra income is not simply about enjoying a larger bank balance.

According to ESPN, she has been putting her money into real estate, purchasing vacation properties in Arizona and making them available as short-term rentals.

Rather than personally managing the properties, Cunningham has brought in a company to handle their operation while she provides the capital.

That arrangement allows her to remain focused on basketball while simultaneously developing an investment portfolio.

Cunningham plans to expand real-estate business

The Fever guard has made it clear that Arizona is only the beginning. Cunningham is considering additional purchases in other popular destinations, including Nashville and Florida.

“I’m about to probably buy one in Nashville and Florida, and so I’m just starting to make a business outside of the court,” Cunningham revealed. “It’s good, it’s fun. I’m trying to buy places that I want to go visit, so when I’m there, I don’t have to pay for it.”

The strategy gives Cunningham several potential benefits. The properties can provide accommodation when she travels for personal reasons, while also offering the possibility of rental income when she isn't using them.

It's also a way for Cunningham to think beyond her playing career.

Professional athletes face an obvious challenge as their earning years in sport are relatively limited. Building assets that can potentially continue generating value after retirement can therefore be an important part of long-term financial planning.

Cunningham has also encouraged other WNBA players to think carefully about what they do with the new money flowing into the league.

Players who spent years operating on much smaller salaries now have considerably more financial freedom, but Cunningham believes that opportunity comes with responsibility.

She explained that athletes need to be “smart with that money,” particularly because many have waited a long time to receive compensation at this level. They “can’t just go out and blow it all or not invest.”

That mindset is particularly notable given Cunningham 's own career path. She was selected by the Phoenix Mercury in the 2019 WNBA Draft after playing college basketball at Missouri and has subsequently established herself as a veteran presence in the league.

Her latest contract also reflects how dramatically the economics of the WNBA are changing. Cunningham 's decision to turn a larger salary into property investments demonstrates one possible way players can use the new financial landscape to create security beyond the court.

“I think it allows all of us to kind of grow and be businesswomen,” the Fever star stated.

For Cunningham , that growth has already begun. With potential properties in Nashville and Florida still on her radar, the $665,000 contract could end up being more than another lucrative season in professional basketball.

It could become another step toward building a business that lasts long after her playing career ends.

articles.title: “The gayest thing you can do”: WNBA star Natasha Cloud lashes out at men who throw sex toys on court
articles.standfirst: The veteran guard said the repeated sex toy stunts reveal how the perpetrators really feel about women
articles.summary: The veteran guard said the repeated sex toy stunts reveal how the perpetrators really feel about women
articles.body:
The final seconds of the Chicago Sky ’s dramatic win over the Golden State Valkyries should have supplied more than enough drama.

Instead, Natasha Cloud left Wintrust Arena talking about something far removed from basketball after another WNBA game was interrupted by sex toys being thrown onto the court.

Multiple objects landed on the floor during the third quarter of Chicago’s 73-70 victory Friday night, briefly stopping play before the Sky eventually won on Sydney Taylor ’s buzzer-beating three-pointer.

Cloud , who scored a team-high 17 points, didn't attempt to hide her anger when the subject came up afterward.

“Y’all lame as f**k,” Cloud said. “In most of these occasions, it’s men. The men that are throwing it, shows that you are weak. Like, extremely weak. And it says a lot about how you feel about women.”

Stunt reflects something deeper

Cloud ’s criticism extended well beyond the disruption itself. She argued that the behavior says more about those responsible than it does about the WNBA or the people they appear to be targeting.

“I’m a firm believer that anyone that has so much of a problem with a marginalized group, just come out and say that you’re a part of our group, because the hate is unwarranted,” she added.

“It says more about the internal struggles of the individual than it ever will say about the collective group.”

Cloud also repeatedly used “gay” as an insult during her remarks while trying to ridicule the men involved, including calling the act of buying a sex toy and throwing it at a women’s basketball game “the gayest thing that you can do.”

Her broader point, however, centered on what she viewed as disrespect toward women and another needless interruption to a league that has already dealt with the same behavior repeatedly.

Friday marked the second consecutive night a WNBA game was disrupted in that fashion. A similar incident occurred during the Atlanta Dream ’s game against the Los Angeles Sparks , where a male suspect was detained after an object was thrown onto the floor.

Dealing with problem that never disappeared

The pattern first became a major league-wide issue during the 2025 season, when sex toys were thrown at games in several cities.

Indiana Fever star Sophie Cunningham was struck by one projectile, while another incident at a New York Liberty game resulted in a 12-year-old fan being hit.

Arrests followed multiple cases, and league officials warned that throwing objects can lead to ejection, lengthy bans and criminal prosecution. Yet those consequences haven't stopped the trend from resurfacing.

Cloud ended her postgame comments by mocking the people responsible and questioning why anyone would spend money on the objects simply to throw them during a basketball game.

Chicago ultimately left with the win, but Cloud ’s frustration made clear that players have grown tired of seeing games interrupted by something they no longer view as harmless attention-seeking.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham hailed as an ‘American Hero’ in wake of debate surrounding women’s sports
articles.standfirst: The Fever star wants basketball to remain the focus while continuing to defend her views
articles.summary: The Fever star wants basketball to remain the focus while continuing to defend her views
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham never expected to become one of the most discussed figures in women’s basketball, but the Indiana Fever guard has found herself at the center of a much larger debate after speaking publicly about transgender participation in women’s sports.

Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom believes Cunningham ’s willingness to share her views has made her an important figure for athletes and fans who feel the same way, calling her an “American hero” during an appearance on Fox News.

“First of all, I want to say she’s an American hero,” Kanter Freedom said. “Everywhere she goes, I see now a lot of people are coming out and actually defending her.”

Kanter Freedom acknowledged that Cunningham has faced criticism since discussing the issue, but said public backlash often follows athletes who take controversial positions.

“Obviously, if you’re standing up for something that you believe in, you’re going to get hate all the time,” he said. “But I think she’s inspiring not only the players in the WNBA but girls from all over the world, not only in America.”

The former NBA center added that he has received messages from supporters internationally asking him to pass along their appreciation if he ever meets Cunningham .

“They’re saying, ‘Hey, if you ever see Sophie, can you please say hi to her?’” he said.

Cunningham becomes a major figure

Cunningham became a prominent voice in the discussion after saying in July that she does not believe transgender women should compete against biological women in female sports.

Her comments quickly drew both support and criticism, turning the Fever guard into a central figure in a wider cultural debate.

The conversation has extended beyond Cunningham ’s original remarks, with supporters organizing rallies around Fever games while others have pushed back in support of transgender inclusion.

The issue has also brought renewed attention to how professional sports leagues handle conversations surrounding gender and competition, even though no transgender woman currently plays in the WNBA.

While the debate has dominated much of the discussion surrounding Cunningham , she has also pushed for greater focus on basketball and the achievements of players on the court.

Speaking about the media attention surrounding the WNBA, Cunningham said athletes are often encouraged to use their platforms but can face criticism when they do.

“People are like, ‘You have a platform. Use it.’ And then, once you use it, it’s like, ‘Go back to playing basketball,’” Cunningham said.

“I think I could do both. Ask me about what’s going on and what I said. And also ask me how great my teammates are doing, how great our team is doing, how great the league is doing.”

Cunningham calls for stronger leadership

Beyond the controversy surrounding her own comments, Cunningham has also spoken about the direction she believes the league should take as it continues to grow.

The Fever guard said the WNBA needs leadership that prioritizes players and the future of the sport.

“I think it needs a person in power who is bold, who is confident, who wants the best for the players and not maybe for themselves all the time,” Cunningham said.

Cunningham ’s position has made her one of the most recognizable names in the current women’s sports conversation. Whether praised or criticized, her comments have ensured that debates around the future of women’s athletics remain firmly in the spotlight.

articles.title: Sydney Taylor sends Chicago into pandemonium with another historic game-winner
articles.summary: Sydney Taylor has done it again and this time the Chicago Sky rookie made WNBA history in the process.
articles.body:
Sydney Taylor has done it again and this time the Chicago Sky rookie made WNBA history in the process.

With the game tied and only seconds remaining against the Golden State Valkyries, Taylor created separation with a crossover and buried a three-pointer with just 0.6 seconds left, giving Chicago a dramatic 73-70 victory.

Then came the celebration. Taylor was immediately surrounded by her teammates as the Sky bench emptied and Wintrust Arena erupted around them. The rookie finished with 14 points and four three-pointers, but none mattered more than the last one.

It was also familiar territory. Taylor had already beaten the Las Vegas Aces with a three-pointer with less than a second remaining earlier this month. Now she is the first rookie in WNBA history to make multiple game-winners with fewer than five seconds left, an extraordinary clutch résumé for a player in her first season.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and Indiana Fever stars steal the spotlight before a bitter night against New York Liberty
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Monique Billings brought three very different styles to a night that ultimately turned difficult for Indiana.
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Monique Billings brought three very different styles to a night that ultimately turned difficult for Indiana.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever's night began with fashion and ended with tension on the court. Before facing New York Liberty at Barclays Center , Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham and Monique Billings arrived in three completely different looks, once again showing off their individual personalities away from the court.

Indiana stayed in the game for much of the night but ultimately fell 109-102 to New York after a tense finish in which every possession could have changed the outcome.

Caitlin Clark kept things simple and elegant

Clark arrived before the game wearing beige jeans , a brown top and brown pointed-toe shoes, completing the look with her hair down.

The Fever star kept things relaxed, without too many accessories or flashy details, while the neutral tones gave her outfit a polished appearance for her arrival at Barclays Center.

Clark carried that presence onto the court and became one of Indiana's main offensive weapons. The guard finished with 21 points, seven assists and four rebounds, while shooting 9-for-18 from the field .

However, her individual performance was not enough to help the Fever come away with the win.

Sophie Cunningham went for a bolder look

Cunningham took a different approach for her arrival. She wore black jeans and a brown top with a jacket-like appearance, pairing the outfit with open-toe shoes and her hair down.

Her look was darker than Clark's, while still maintaining the casual feel that defined Indiana's pregame arrivals.

On the court, Cunningham also found a way to contribute. She finished with 10 points, five assists and two steals after making four of her five shots .

Monique Billings brought the most color

Billings delivered the most eye-catching look of the three . She arrived in a blue mini dress covered in yellow and white flowers, paired with a pink handbag and a sunflower accessory.

White heels, her hair down and pink flower earrings completed a much more colorful outfit than those chosen by her teammates.

Her night on the court, however, proved much more difficult. Billings finished with four points, two rebounds, one assist and one steal in 14 minutes .

Foul trouble limited her impact. She picked up five personal fouls and fouled out of the game, while also missing two free throws in the fourth quarter.

The Fever will have to bounce back quickly

Indiana will not have much time to dwell on the disappointing result. On Sunday, August 23, the Fever will return to action against the Chicago Sky at Wintrust Arena .

White heels, her hair down and pink flower earrings completed a much more colorful outfit than those chosen by her teammates.
Her night on the court, however, proved much more difficult. Billings finished with four points, two rebounds, one assist and one steal in 14 minutes .
Foul trouble limited her impact. She picked up five personal fouls and fouled out of the game, while also missing two free throws in the fourth quarter.
The Fever will have to bounce back quickly
Indiana will not have much time to dwell on the disappointing result. On Sunday, August 23, the Fever will return to action against the Chicago Sky at Wintrust Arena .
