articles.title: The impressive mark set by Olivia Miles that left Caitlin Clark behind
articles.standfirst: Minnesota's player's performance against Washington ended up adding another notable milestone to the great season the Lynx point guard is having.
articles.summary: Minnesota's player's performance against Washington ended up adding another notable milestone to the great season the Lynx point guard is having.
articles.body:
O livia Mile s continues to rack up historic numbers; this time she not only reached a milestone but also put her name alongside one of the greatest figures who revolutionized the WNBA.

Minnesota's guard reached 700 points and 200 assists in just 36 games, while Clark needed 37 games to reach those same figures during her rookie campaign. The difference is minimal, but enough for Miles to take the title from Clark and become the fastest to achieve it.

Olivia Miles surpasses Caitlin Clark in a WNBA record

After a 24-point, seven-assist performance against the Washington Mystics, Miles left the game not only with a win alongside her team, but also claiming a new place in WNBA history.

Miles was one of the key players in Minnesota's 94-84 victory, and with those numbers she officially reached the two marks she needed to surpass Clark.

Caitlin had managed in that first 2024 season to reach 700 points and 200 assists in a total of 37 games, while Olivia did it in one fewer game.

What is most interesting is that the record Clark just lost might not be the last one. Miles already has 720 points and has six more games to increase that total . Clark had finished her first season with 769 points, so she needs only 50 points to surpass that mark. And with an average of 20 points per game, Clark's record appears closer and closer.

The picture changes drastically when we talk about assists; the gap is still considerable: Indiana's star finished her rookie season with 337, while Miles has 222.

Thus, what began as a comparison between a young rising star and one of the WNBA’s biggest stars is already starting to make its way into the record books. Olivia Miles has just taken a record away from Caitlin Clark and, with the season still ongoing, it might not be the last.

articles.title: Is Caitlin Clark burning out? The Fever star makes a concerning confession amid the losing streak
articles.standfirst: Indiana’s superstar admits fatigue is affecting the entire team as the Fever enter the final stretch of the regular season
articles.summary: Indiana’s superstar admits fatigue is affecting the entire team as the Fever enter the final stretch of the regular season
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark has acknowledged that fatigue is becoming a reality for the Indiana Fever as they navigate a demanding stretch of the WNBA schedule, but the superstar does not want tired legs to become an excuse for the team's recent struggles.

Indiana suffered its second consecutive defeat on Saturday, falling 109-102 to the New York Liberty at Barclays Center.

The loss came just days after the Fever were beaten 91-85 by the Dallas Wings, extending a difficult portion of a five-game road trip.

Clark was productive against New York, finishing with 21 points, four rebounds and seven assists while continuing to serve as the primary creator for the Fever. Kelsey Mitchell led Indiana with 25 points, while Aliyah Boston added 22.

Makayla Timpson and Sophie Cunningham also reached double figures with 10 points apiece.

Despite the result, Clark refused to point toward Indiana's schedule as the reason for the defeat.

“There’s no excuses,” she said. “Yeah, our schedule’s tough. And I think we play more back-to-backs than just about anybody in the league. But it is what it is.”

That assessment is particularly relevant with the Fever facing another quick turnaround. Indiana was scheduled to travel to Chicago to face the Sky on the second night of a back-to-back, leaving little time for the players to recover from the physical demands of the Liberty game.

Caitlin Clark delivers blunt message on Fever fatigue

Clark did not pretend that the demanding schedule was having no effect on the team. Instead, she admitted that tiredness and soreness are being felt throughout the roster.

“Yeah, everybody’s tired,” Clark acknowledged. “Everybody’s sore. Who cares? Figure out a way to make yourself feel better and suit up and go play.”

The comments provide an insight into the physical challenge facing Indiana at a crucial point of the season. The Fever have already secured their place in the playoffs for the third consecutive season, but their position in the standings remains important with the postseason approaching.

Indiana dropped to 24-14 following the defeat to New York and remained the No. 5 seed with six games left. That means every remaining contest carries significance as teams jockey for playoff positioning.

Clark nevertheless tried to frame the immediate challenge positively, rather than dwelling on the consecutive defeats.

“Chicago’s playing really good basketball,” she continued. “I think for us, you have to look at it in a positive way. We’re coming off of a loss. It’s a great opportunity for us to go and finish this road trip with a win. That’s how I see it.”

The matchup with Chicago also carries an additional layer of intrigue because it represents the first meeting between the two teams since an incident involving Cunningham and Sky forward DiJonai Carrington .

During their previous encounter, Carrington attempted to challenge Cunningham on a breakaway layup but made contact with her face. The incident resulted in a Flagrant Foul 2 and added considerable tension to the matchup.

Carrington has subsequently indicated that she is looking forward to the next meeting, adding another storyline to an already demanding game for the Fever.

For Clark , however, the immediate priority is simply getting through a grueling stretch of the schedule.

The Fever are already guaranteed postseason basketball, but their recent losses demonstrate that reaching the playoffs and entering them in strong form are two very different challenges.

Clark's admission that “everybody’s tired” is therefore worth noting, but it does not necessarily indicate that she or the Fever are falling apart. Instead, it highlights the reality of a long WNBA season, particularly for a team still fighting for the best possible position heading into the postseason.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark steals the hearts of her youngest fans again with a moment that says it all
articles.standfirst: The Indiana Fever star offered another glimpse of the connection she has built with young basketball fans.
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever star offered another glimpse of the connection she has built with young basketball fans.
articles.body:
Yesterday, the Indiana Fever had a date at Barclays Center to face the New York Liberty in a tough matchup that ended in a 109-102 loss for Caitlin Clark’s team . The point guard responded with 21 points and seven assists in 35 minutes , while also surpassing the franchise’s three-point record and moving into fourth place in Indiana history in that category.

But amid everything that happened that night, one image ended up showing something far beyond the final score: the enormous influence Clark has on her youngest fans . In a video that recently began circulating, several young girls wearing basketball jerseys can be seen near the tunnel, waiting for their chance to meet her.

And although the wait probably felt endless, when that special moment finally arrived, their reactions said everything. Their faces lit up with a mix of happiness and excitement as they finally had Clark standing right in front of them .

Indiana ends road trip as Clark stuns in style

Indiana is currently facing the Chicago Sky at Wintrust Arena in the final game of its five-game road trip .

For the occasion, Clark once again made an impression during the pregame . The Indiana star arrived wearing Nike pants, a white sweatshirt, matching white sneakers and headphones, while her long hair completed a simple and comfortable look before taking the court.

Will they be able to come away with the win today?

articles.title: Caitlin Clark destroys DiJonai Carrington and she has a very dangerous reaction
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark buried a clutch 3 over DiJonai Carrington—and what happened seconds later stole the spotlight.
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark buried a clutch 3 over DiJonai Carrington—and what happened seconds later stole the spotlight.
articles.body:
The highly anticipated showdown between the Indiana Fever and Chicago Sky turned up the heat on one of the WNBA 's fastest-growing rivalries, with Caitlin Clark and DiJonai Carrington taking center stage in another heated chapter.

The game remained tightly contested throughout the first half, with Chicago taking a slim 51-50 lead into the break. Much of the attention, however, was focused on the rematch between Carrington and Sophie Cunningham following their controversial Aug. 8 incident , when the Sky guard was ejected just three minutes into the game after being assessed a Flagrant 2 foul for a collision with Cunningham.

But it was Caitlin Clark who ultimately stole the spotlight

Midway through the second quarter, the Fever star found herself isolated against Carrington, stepped back, and buried a 3-pointer right over her defender . The shot ignited the crowd and set up the game's most talked-about moment.

Seconds later, as both players ran back on defense, Carrington intentionally bumped into Clark. The Indiana guard responded with a calm but telling gesture, brushing Carrington aside with a simple flick of her hand and completely dismissing the attempted provocation.

The exchange marked the first physical confrontation between the two players and quickly went viral across social media.

Although Indiana and Chicago have never shared a particularly heated rivalry, Clark's arrival has completely changed the dynamic between the two franchises. And judging by the way s he responded to Carrington, the Fever superstar sent a clear message: she has no intention of being intimidated.

articles.title: Why was Enes Kanter ejected from the WNBA game between the Indiana Fever and Chicago Sky?
articles.standfirst: The Fever-Sky rivalry delivered another headline — but this time, the drama came from courtside after Enes Kanter Freedom’s confrontation with Natasha Cloud.
articles.summary: The Fever-Sky rivalry delivered another headline — but this time, the drama came from courtside after Enes Kanter Freedom’s confrontation with Natasha Cloud.
articles.body:
E nes Kanter Freedom found himself at the center of controversy once again. The former NBA player, who has expressed his intention to make his way into women’s basketball, was removed from Wintrust Arena during the third quarter of Sunday’s matchup between the Chicago Sky and Indiana Fever after a heated exchange with Chicago guard Natasha Cloud .

The incident occurred while the Fever held an 81-75 lead during a timeout. From the court, Cloud began directing comments toward Freedom, who was seated courtside.

The former center responded and stepped toward the floor, prompting security personnel to intervene and escort him out of the arena as Sky fans booed him.

Minutes after being removed, Freedom reacted on X , claiming he was kicked out for supporting women’s sports.

“I just got kicked out of a @WNBA game for supporting WOMEN! Let that sink in, AMERICA!”

“It’s always women hating on other women.”

The confrontation carried a political backdrop. Freedom had previously criticized Cloud over some of her comments about the United States and said he would buy her a ticket to China, Russia, or Turkey so she could see “what real tyranny looks like.” He also attended the game wearing a shirt featuring the definition of the word “woman,” a message that sparked reactions among those in attendance.

The former player had already created controversy before the game. During halftime, he posted a photo outside a restroom inside the arena with the caption:

“It’s halftime and I need to use the restroom… Rules are rules @WNBA.”

Tensions were also high before tipoff, when Freedom was confronted by a group of protesters outside the arena. Security had to create a perimeter around the 6-foot-10 former NBA center , while some fans made offensive gestures and others shouted, “You were trash in the league!”

Freedom shared a video of the confrontation on social media with the message:

“We are getting attacked before the @WNBA game in Chicago.”

In recent months, Freedom has become a controversial figure due to his outspoken views in defense of women’s sports and his support for players such as Sophie Cunningham.

For now, the WNBA has not announced whether there will be additional consequences or whether Freedom will be allowed to attend future games.

On the court, the Indiana Fever earned a dominant victory, defeating the Chicago Sky 113-90.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark leaves fans stunned after pre-game encounter with Robert Lewandowski
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark and Robert Lewandowski shared a special crossover moment before the Fever-Sky showdown.
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and Robert Lewandowski shared a special crossover moment before the Fever-Sky showdown.
articles.body:
Every now and then, the WNBA crosses paths with other major sports worlds, creating unique moments. Over the years, we have seen star athletes meet, unexpected friendships develop, and gestures that transcend beyond a single sport.

On Sunday night, two of the most recognizable names in global sports crossed paths before the matchup between the Indiana Fever and the Chicago Sky . WNBA sensation Caitlin Clark and Chicago Fire forward Robert Lewandowski shared a photo that quickly caught the attention of fans.

The Polish striker took advantage of his proximity to attend the game and watch one of the biggest stars in women’s basketball face his city’s WNBA team. Lewandowski, one of the biggest names in MLS , did not want to miss the opportunity to see Clark and the Fever in action.

Both athletes represent two of the most popular figures in their respective sports, making the meeting a notable crossover between the worlds of soccer and women’s basketball .

A meeting between two superstars

Since being selected as the No. 1 overall pick in the 2024 WNBA Draft , Clark has established herself as one of the league’s biggest stars. The former Iowa standout entered the league after a historic college career and has played a key role in elevating the popularity of the Indiana Fever and the WNBA to unprecedented levels.

Meanwhile, Lewandowski has built one of the most impressive careers in modern soccer. The Polish striker is regarded as one of the best goal scorers of his generation and made his mark with clubs such as Borussia Dortmund, Bayern Munich, and Barcelona before joining the Chicago Fire .

At 37 years old, the Polish national team captain remains an international icon and is his country’s all-time leading scorer. His presence in Chicago provides MLS fans another opportunity to see one of the biggest stars in world sports up close.

Although Clark and Lewandowski compete in completely different disciplines, their global impact made this encounter a perfect blend of two sporting worlds. The photo shared by the Fever gave fans from both the WNBA and soccer a memorable moment before the game tipped off.

For one night in Chicago, two global superstars met away from their respective fields and created an image that will likely remain in fans’ memories.

articles.title: Does Ted Lasso want to “sign” Caitlin Clark for the next season? Jason Sudeikis got all the fans excited
articles.standfirst: The Ted Lasso star watched Caitlin Clark deliver a spectacular performance for the Indiana Fever, prompting fans to imagine a very different kind of crossover
articles.summary: The Ted Lasso star watched Caitlin Clark deliver a spectacular performance for the Indiana Fever, prompting fans to imagine a very different kind of crossover
articles.body:
J ason Sudeikis has given Ted Lasso fans another reason to dream about the future after showing his support for Caitlin Clark during the Indiana Fever 's meeting with the Chicago Sky .

Sudeikis, who plays the relentlessly optimistic football coach at the heart of Apple's hit comedy, was in attendance as Clark produced one of the best performances of her young WNBA career.

The Fever cruised to a 113-90 victory on Sunday, with Clark exploding for 37 points and 10 assists.

She also knocked down a career-best eight three-pointers, helping Indiana set a franchise record with 18 made threes. The performance came at the end of a demanding five-game road trip and gave the Fever a much-needed response after consecutive defeats.

Sudeikis ' presence naturally caught the attention of fans, particularly because of the timing. The fourth season of Ted Lasso recently returned to Apple TV+, and the show has undergone a significant change for its latest chapter.

Rather than concentrating solely on the men's team at AFC Richmond , the new season follows Ted as he takes charge of a second-division women's football team. Apple confirmed that the season premiered on August 5, with new episodes arriving weekly through October 7.

That change in direction made Sudeikis ' appearance at a WNBA game particularly amusing for supporters.

The idea of Clark somehow becoming part of the Ted Lasso universe quickly became an attractive fantasy for fans.

While there is no indication that Sudeikis or Apple TV are actually attempting to recruit Clark for the series, his enthusiastic support created plenty of speculation about what a collaboration between the two stars could look like.

Could Caitlin Clark really become part of the Ted Lasso universe?

The obvious obstacle is that Ted Lasso remains a football show. Clark is one of basketball's biggest stars, and there is no suggestion that she is preparing to trade the Fever for AFC Richmond.

But the timing makes the fan speculation easy to understand.

Season four is already exploring women's sport through the fictional Lady Greyhounds. The storyline allows the show to examine the different pressures faced by female athletes while retaining the optimism and humour that made the original series popular.

Reuters described the new season as an exploration of women's sport, including issues involving resources, facilities and expectations placed on female athletes.

Clark would therefore fit naturally into the show's broader cultural conversation about women's athletics, even if she never appears as a player.

And there is certainly no shortage of star power surrounding the Fever guard.

Against Chicago, Clark became only the fifth player in WNBA history to record a game with at least 30 points and 10 assists for the fifth time in her career.

articles.title: Natasha Cloud's message following her argument with Enes Kanter Freedom makes her stance on transgender people clear
articles.standfirst: The Chicago Sky guard made her position known after a heated courtside confrontation with the former NBA player during Indiana's 113-90 win
articles.summary: The Chicago Sky guard made her position known after a heated courtside confrontation with the former NBA player during Indiana's 113-90 win
articles.body:
N atasha Cloud made her position on transgender people unmistakably clear after becoming involved in a heated confrontation with former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom during the Chicago Sky 's loss to the Indiana Fever .

The incident occurred Sunday at Wintrust Arena during a game that was already carrying significant attention because of Freedom's recent campaign to enter the WNBA .

The former NBA center was sitting along the baseline wearing a black shirt displaying the definition of a woman as “WOMAN noun. adult human female.”

Late in the third quarter, Cloud scored a basket with 1:22 remaining. After celebrating with teammate Aicha Coulibaly , the Chicago guard turned toward Freedom and began yelling and pointing in his direction.

Freedom stood up and moved one step toward the court, prompting security personnel and Sky players to immediately separate the pair.

Freedom was subsequently escorted from the arena and did not return for the remainder of the contest.

The precise words exchanged between the two were initially unclear. Cloud did not speak to reporters after the game, but she later posted a message on Threads that made her position on transgender people clear.

"To every trans kid/person, You are apart of MY community & tribe. You belong. You’re loved. You’re seen. You’re perfect as you are. & you will always be protected by me," Cloud wrote.

The statement was widely interpreted as a response to the controversy surrounding Freedom's presence at the game and his public campaign over transgender participation in women's sports.

Cloud receives support from her Chicago teammates

Cloud's comments came after an emotionally charged night for the Sky, who were beaten 113-90 by Indiana. The game itself became secondary to the confrontation, with Cloud subsequently meeting with both team and league security.

Chicago coach Tyler Marsh nevertheless made it clear that he supported his veteran guard.

“I told her she wasn’t,” Marsh said when discussing Cloud's concern that the confrontation had become a distraction.

“I told her that we all embrace her as someone that protects our team and protects people that need to be protected and so Tash is always going to stand on that, and we stand for Tash.”

The coach also suggested that Freedom's presence should not have overshadowed the players and the basketball itself.

“If you come to a game you should probably come to enjoy the basketball,” Marsh said, “and that seems pretty simple to me. I think these players deserve that and have earned that. Being a former basketball player, you should probably understand and feel that too.”

The confrontation comes amid a broader debate surrounding gender eligibility in women's sports. Freedom has publicly said he intends to pursue a place in the WNBA, while former NBA player Royce White has also made a similar declaration.

The WNBA's collective bargaining agreement states that only women are eligible to play in the league, although the agreement does not spell out a detailed policy concerning gender identity.

Freedom had attended the game after previously making his views on the issue known and had also appeared at a rally supporting Indiana Fever player Sophie Cunningham , who has publicly expressed opposition to transgender women competing in women's sports.

After being removed from the arena, Freedom offered his own version of events on social media.

"I just got kicked out of a @WNBA game for supporting WOMEN! Let that sink in, AMERICA!" he wrote on X.

He followed that with another message: "It’s always women hating on other women," he wrote.

Cloud , meanwhile, chose not to engage in a lengthy public back-and-forth. Instead, her message focused on transgender people and her promise of support.

That distinction is significant. Whatever caused the initial exchange between the two, Cloud's subsequent statement left little ambiguity about where she stands on the treatment of transgender people.

For the Sky guard, the controversy has become another example of how quickly discussions away from the basketball court can become intertwined with the WNBA.

Her coach has publicly backed her, while Freedom has continued to use the incident as part of a much larger argument about women's sports.

For now, though, the clearest message from Cloud came after the confrontation, and it was directed not at Freedom, but at transgender people she wanted to reassure that they belong and are supported.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark predicted that Stephanie White would have a great night and revealed her secret to playing better
articles.standfirst: The Fever superstar backed up her pregame confidence with a career-best shooting display as Indiana ended its difficult road trip with a statement victory
articles.summary: The Fever superstar backed up her pregame confidence with a career-best shooting display as Indiana ended its difficult road trip with a statement victory
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark apparently knew she was in for a special night before she even stepped onto the court.

The Indiana Fever superstar produced one of the finest performances of her young WNBA career on Sunday, scoring 37 points and dishing out 10 assists as Indiana overwhelmed the Chicago Sky 113-90.

Clark also knocked down a career-high eight three-pointers, helping the Fever recover from consecutive defeats and finish a demanding five-game road trip with a victory.

What made the performance particularly interesting was Clark's admission after the final buzzer. Speaking to NBC Sports' Ashley ShahAhmadi , the three-time All-Star revealed that she had already told head coach Stephanie White that she expected to have a big game.

“Before the game started,” Clark said. “You can ask Coach Steph. I said it’s going to be one of those nights.” That prediction proved remarkably accurate.

Clark was efficient throughout the contest, shooting 13-of-24 from the field while adding three rebounds and a steal. Her eight made threes represented a new career high and contributed to an Indiana franchise record of 18 three-pointers in the game.

The performance was exactly what Indiana needed after the Fever had lost to the Dallas Wings and New York Liberty on consecutive nights. Sunday's victory improved the Fever to 25-14 and gave them an important boost heading toward the final stretch of the regular season.

But Clark's explanation for why she felt so good was considerably simpler than any complicated tactical adjustment.

Clark credits a much-needed night's sleep

After spending much of the season dealing with an exhausting schedule, Clark suggested that rest was one of the biggest reasons she felt so sharp against Chicago.

“I think I just got some really good sleep at the hotel last night from 3:00 a.m. to about 11:00 a.m.,” she added. “So I got nice hours, woke up, watched a film, went through the scout and came and played.”

The timing was significant. The Fever were playing their third game in four nights and were finishing a five-game road trip, circumstances that had already prompted Clark to acknowledge that fatigue was affecting the team.

Instead of allowing the workload to show, however, Clark looked energized against Chicago.

Her 37 points were complemented by 10 assists, making it the fifth game of her career in which she has reached at least 30 points and 10 assists. According to the Fever, Clark now has more such games than the rest of the WNBA has combined, with the rest of the league having four.

Kelsey Mitchell also produced a huge performance, scoring 30 points as Indiana's backcourt overwhelmed Chicago. The two guards combined for 67 points, while the Fever compensated for the absence of Aliyah Boston , who was sidelined with a right leg injury.

The victory also provided a response to questions about whether Indiana's exhausting schedule was beginning to catch up with the team. Clark's performance suggested that, at least for one night, the Fever still had plenty in the tank.

There was also a clear element of preparation behind the spectacular shooting display. Clark described waking up, studying film and going through the scouting report before arriving at the arena.

That combination of recovery and preparation appeared to work perfectly.

White, meanwhile, received a front-row view of the player who had predicted her own breakout performance hours earlier.

The Fever coach has increasingly relied on Clark to orchestrate Indiana's offense, and Sunday's display showed just how dangerous the team can be when its star guard is operating at full speed.

The Fever now have some valuable breathing room after completing their road trip, with the schedule providing an opportunity to recover before their next matchup.

And if Clark can continue to pair proper rest with the kind of preparation she described in Chicago, Indiana's opponents may have plenty to worry about when the playoffs arrive.

articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom receives a serious warning from a Former NFL player who adores Caitlin Clark: “He's doing more harm to women”
articles.standfirst: Robert Griffin III criticized the former NBA player after his confrontation with Natasha Cloud during the Fever-Sky game
articles.summary: Robert Griffin III criticized the former NBA player after his confrontation with Natasha Cloud during the Fever-Sky game
articles.body:
E nes Kanter Freedom 's latest appearance at a WNBA game has sparked another wave of controversy, this time drawing a pointed response from former NFL quarterback Robert Griffin III .

Freedom was ejected from Sunday's Indiana Fever-Chicago Sky matchup at Wintrust Arena after a confrontation with Chicago guard Natasha Cloud .

The incident occurred late in the third quarter, shortly after Cloud scored a basket and directed her frustration toward Freedom , who was sitting courtside.

Freedom stood up and moved toward the court before security personnel stepped between the two. He was subsequently escorted from the arena and did not return for the remainder of the game.

The former NBA player was wearing a shirt that read, “WOMAN noun. adult human female.”

The confrontation quickly became part of the wider debate surrounding gender eligibility in women's sports, a subject Freedom has increasingly made central to his public appearances and social-media activity.

Griffin , who has been outspoken in his support of Caitlin Clark and women's basketball, did not hold back when reacting to the incident.

“Enes Kanter is causing more harm and damage to the women he claims he is trying to protect. THIS is lame.”

Griffin followed that post with another criticism of the growing focus on controversies surrounding the WNBA.

“EVERYTHING but basketball is leading the conversation about the WNBA and it’s a disservice to the incredible women playing night in and night out.”

Why Freedom has become involved in the WNBA debate

Freedom's involvement in the issue did not begin with Sunday's confrontation.

The former NBA center has recently aligned himself with Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham , who has expressed concerns about transgender athletes competing in women's sports.

Cunningham previously said she wanted to “protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men.”

Freedom has repeatedly expressed his support for Cunningham and has attempted to position his activism as a defense of women's athletics.

He went even further by declaring himself eligible for the 2027 WNBA Draft alongside former NBA player Royce White , saying they identify as women. The announcement was widely viewed as a provocative extension of the argument he has been making about eligibility rules in women's sports.

That activism has now brought Freedom into direct conflict with players and fans at WNBA venues.

According to reports surrounding Sunday's game, it was not immediately clear exactly what Cloud and Freedom were saying to each other before security intervened.

Cloud did not speak to the media during the Sky's postgame availability, but later posted a message on Threads directed toward transgender people.

"To every trans kid/person, You are apart of MY community & tribe. You belong. You’re loved. You’re seen. You’re perfect as you are. & you will always be protected by me," Cloud wrote.

The exchange occurred during a game that already carried plenty of attention because of the Fever-Sky rivalry and Indiana's Caitlin Clark -led lineup. Instead of the basketball taking center stage, however, the confrontation became one of the night's biggest talking points.

That is precisely what Griffin objected to.

His argument was not simply about Freedom's views, but about how the confrontation and surrounding activism could shift attention away from the athletes competing on the floor.

Freedom's NBA career gives him considerable name recognition. The Utah Jazz selected him third overall in the 2011 NBA Draft, and he went on to spend 11 seasons with six teams, including the Jazz, Oklahoma City Thunder, New York Knicks, Portland Trail Blazers and Boston Celtics.

His playing career ended in 2022, but he has remained highly visible through political and social activism.

Now, Griffin is warning that the strategy Freedom is using to promote his views could ultimately undermine the very athletes he says he wants to defend.

For the WNBA, the episode represents another example of how debates outside basketball can become intertwined with the league's games. And with Freedom promising to remain involved in the conversation, the dispute is unlikely to disappear anytime soon.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham finds herself back at center of controversy even when staying silent
articles.standfirst: A courtside confrontation in Chicago reignited debate over Cunningham’s role in the league’s culture-war controversy
articles.summary: A courtside confrontation in Chicago reignited debate over Cunningham’s role in the league’s culture-war controversy
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham barely figured in the box score Sunday, yet she still became one of the biggest names in the conversation after the Indiana Fever ’s 110-93 WNBA win over the Chicago Sky .

The Fever guard played only 10 minutes and scored three points, but a courtside confrontation involving former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom and Sky guard Natasha Cloud quickly pulled Cunningham back into the league’s ongoing debate over transgender participation in women’s sports.

Kanter attended the game at Wintrust Arena wearing a black shirt featuring a definition of a woman and had earlier appeared at an XX-XY rally opposing transgender inclusion in the WNBA.

During the game, Cloud directed words toward him following a tough layup, Kanter responded from his courtside seat and he was later removed from the arena.

Cunningham was nowhere near the exchange. Still, some WNBA fans and reporters argued that the broader atmosphere surrounding the incident can be traced back to comments she made in July.

“Multiple WNBA players and the league itself have been under attack for over a month, and Sophie Cunningham is at the center of it,” one WNBA reporter wrote on social media.

Why Cunningham is being blamed

The criticism centers on Cunningham ’s earlier comments that transgender women should not compete against biological women in women’s sports.

Her remarks quickly became part of a much larger national debate, drawing support from conservative commentators and activists while also prompting strong opposition from people who viewed the discussion as hostile toward transgender athletes.

No transgender woman currently plays in the WNBA, but rallies and counterprotests have increasingly become part of the atmosphere surrounding Fever games.

“This league has let Sophie Cunningham destroy what was supposed to be an inclusive environment, but Cloud’s willingness to fight against that is refreshing,” one fan wrote after Sunday’s incident.

Another added: “ Cunningham needs to be asked targeted questions about this until she takes accountability for what she’s brought to the league.”

Some reactions were far more extreme. One fan called for Cunningham to receive a lifetime ban, despite there being no indication that she violated any league rule in connection with the incident.

There is no evidence Cunningham encouraged Kanter to attend the game, participate in the rally or confront Cloud .

Kanter removal pushes debate even further

Kanter had been posting updates from his day before the game, including footage from the rally and his arrival at the arena.

The former NBA center has also repeatedly used his proposed 2027 WNBA Draft campaign as a satirical way to criticize gender eligibility rules, publicly describing himself as a woman for the purpose of making that political point.

After being removed, Kanter claimed Cloud ’s response demonstrated that “women don’t support women.”

The confrontation gave Cunningham ’s critics another reason to argue that her initial comments helped move the WNBA into an increasingly polarized culture-war debate.

“This is on Sophie Cunningham , and I will not be explaining any further,” another WNBA reporter wrote.

That remains an opinion rather than an established fact. Cunningham wasn't part of Sunday’s confrontation, but her remarks have unquestionably become a recurring reference point whenever the debate follows the Fever .

What began as one player’s answer about women’s sports has now become a league-wide conversation that is increasingly difficult to separate from what happens on the court.

The confrontation gave Cunningham ’s critics another reason to argue that her initial comments helped move the WNBA into an increasingly polarized culture-war debate.
“This is on Sophie Cunningham , and I will not be explaining any further,” another WNBA reporter wrote.

That remains an opinion rather than an established fact. Cunningham wasn't part of Sunday’s confrontation, but her remarks have unquestionably become a recurring reference point whenever the debate follows the Fever .
What began as one player’s answer about women’s sports has now become a league-wide conversation that is increasingly difficult to separate from what happens on the court.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark makes WNBA history again with a mark the rest of the league has never matched combined
articles.standfirst: Clark continues to make a case for MVP with unprecedented stat lines and records in the WNBA
articles.summary: Clark continues to make a case for MVP with unprecedented stat lines and records in the WNBA
articles.body:
While we are just one month away from the final stretch of the 30th WNBA regular season , seven teams have already officially punched their tickets to the playoffs , leaving only a single postseason spot up for grabs, a race currently leaning toward the Dallas Wings over the expansion Portland Fire .

Most squads have only five to seven games remaining on their schedules, a compressed timeline driven by a major league-wide pause: following the games this upcoming Sunday, the WNBA will halt play from August 31 through September 16 , to accommodate the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, Germany.

During this international showcase, 12 marquee stars, including Caitlin Clark , A'ja Wilson , Paige Bueckers , and Breanna Stewart , will represent their countries in Group D, facing China on September 4th, Italy on September 6th, and Czechia on September 7th.

The group winner will advance directly to the Quarterfinals on September 10 , with the Semifinals slated for September 12 and the Championship Game on September 13 .

Caitlin Clark Shatters More Records With Mind-Boggling Performance

As the league enters its final chapter, the MVP race remains wide open, featuring four-time winner and scoring leader A'ja Wilson as the favorite, closely trailed by rookie sensation Olivia Miles , who has steered the league's top-performing team, and Caitlin Clark , who is putting together the most offensively productive season in league history while ranking third in points per game (22.1 PPG) and first in assists (8.3 APG) .

Following the Indiana Fever's dominant 113-90 victory over the Chicago Sky , Clark massively boosted her MVP stock by exploding for 37 points , a career-high eight three-pointers , and 10 assists.

This milestone marked the fifth game of her career with 30+ points and 10+ assists , a staggering statistic meaning she alone has more such games than the rest of WNBA history combined (4 games) .

Unquestionably, she is operating on a plane entirely unseen before in women's professional basketball. Fueled by this historic production, the Fever offense is averaging 96.6 PPG , the highest mark ever recorded in a single season, and has eclipsed the 100-point threshold in 18 of their 39 games , shattering the all-time single-season record for most triple-digit scoring outings.

While these video-game numbers heavily bolster Clark's MVP candidacy , she faces fierce competition down the stretch from Wilson, who continues to lead the league in scoring (26.0 PPG) while anchoring defenses with a league-leading 2.0 blocks per game.

articles.title: Enes Kanter confirms what Natasha Cloud said about Sophie Cunningham before he was ejected
articles.standfirst: The former NBA center says a simple celebration sparked the courtside exchange that ended with his removal
articles.summary: The former NBA center says a simple celebration sparked the courtside exchange that ended with his removal
articles.body:
Enes Kanter Freedom says one of the biggest controversies from Sunday’s Fever-Sky game began with something entirely ordinary: Sophie Cunningham making a 3-pointer.

Kanter , attending his first WNBA game from courtside at Wintrust Arena, claims he raised his hands to celebrate the Indiana Fever guard’s shot late in the third quarter.

Moments later, according to his account, Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud turned toward him and made a pointed remark involving Cunningham .

“Sophie Cunningham shot a three, and I put my hands up to celebrate,” Kanter said in an interview with Fox News. “Literally, a couple possessions later, Natasha came back and started screaming and yelling and said, ‘She’s not gonna sleep with you.’”

The exchange quickly escalated, with Kanter and Cloud trading words before security eventually escorted the former NBA center from the arena. Cloud has not publicly confirmed that she made the specific remark Kanter attributed to her.

Kanter tried to explain support for Cunningham

Kanter said he responded by telling Cloud that his reaction had nothing to do with any personal interest in Cunningham .

“I was like, ‘I am not trying to sleep with her. I’m just here to protect women and support her,’” Kanter said.

“And then, obviously, after that she started yapping, and she started to walk towards me,” Kanter added. “She started to use some very heavy language. She started to actually cuss, and I was very shocked.”

Kanter also criticized the language he says was used in front of younger fans.

“I cannot believe that she was just cussing and just using those F-bombs in front of all these kids,” he said.

The confrontation drew even more attention because of Kanter ’s increasingly public role in the debate over transgender participation in women’s sports.

He has repeatedly backed Cunningham ’s view that transgender women should not compete against biological women in women’s competition and has even declared himself eligible for the 2027 WNBA Draft as part of a satirical protest.

Natasha Cloud answers controversy

Cloud didn't directly respond to Kanter ’s version of the exchange afterward. Instead, she posted a message on Threads aimed at transgender people.

“To every trans kid/person, you are a part of MY community & tribe. You belong. You’re loved. You’re seen. You’re perfect as you are. & you will always be protected by me,” Cloud wrote.

That response underlined how far the incident had moved beyond basketball. Cunningham herself wasn't involved in the confrontation.

Her only connection to the moment was the shot Kanter says prompted him to celebrate, but her earlier comments on transgender participation have made her a recurring reference point in the broader debate surrounding the league.

The result was another game in which a basketball moment became secondary to a culture-war controversy that continues to follow the WNBA.

The former NBA center argued against the decision before security escorted him away from his courtside seat.

Kanter had already drawn attention by wearing a shirt reading “WOMAN noun. Adult human female,” amid his ongoing criticism of transgender eligibility in women's basketball.

He came to watch a WNBA game. He ended up becoming one of its biggest moments.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark has the last word after DiJonai Carrington tries to rattle her
articles.summary: DiJonai Carrington appeared to try to get under Caitlin Clark's skin, but the Fever superstar had a pretty simple response.
articles.body:
DiJonai Carrington appeared to try to get under Caitlin Clark's skin, but the Fever superstar had a pretty simple response.

During Sunday night's game, Carrington appeared to shove Clark after the play. But instead of escalating the situation, Clark turned around, gave her a dismissive “whatever” gesture and went straight back to business.

And then she answered on the scoreboard.

Clark exploded for 37 points, a career-high eight three-pointers and 10 assists as Indiana eliminated Chicago from playoff contention.

Carrington may have tried to rattle her, but Clark let her game have the last word.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham reacts when photographer asks her to do her signature finger point
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham's finger point has become so famous that apparently she can't even walk down the street without someone asking her to do it.
articles.body: Sophie Cunningham's finger point has become so famous that apparently she can't even walk down the street without someone asking her to do it. It all started during a June game against Phoenix, when Cunningham silently pointed at DeWanna Bonner for 22 straight seconds during a heated exchange. The bizarre moment exploded online and quickly became one of the year's biggest WNBA memes. Since then, fans have constantly asked Cunningham to recreate it. At her own youth basketball camp, kids even used the signature point while taking pictures with her. But this time was different. As Cunningham left a building, someone who appeared to be a photographer shouted, “Sophie, do the pointing!” Apparently, Sophie will do the point for her young fans. Paparazzi? Not so much.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham refuses to back down as WNBA controversy continues to grow
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham has become one of the most outspoken figures in the debate surrounding transgender athletes in women's basketball, and she says the backlash isn't changing who she is.
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has become one of the most outspoken figures in the debate surrounding transgender athletes in women's basketball, and she says the backlash isn't changing who she is.

The Fever star explained that trying to satisfy everyone is impossible, saying she's “100% okay and happy and at peace” with who she is.

She acknowledged there's always room to grow and become better, but made it clear she's comfortable speaking her mind even when it brings criticism.

Her comments come as the WNBA finds itself at the center of an increasingly heated national debate over transgender eligibility in women's sports. Commissioner Cathy Engelbert has called the issue complex and said the league will continue discussions with players and team leaders.

For Cunningham, though, the message is simple: she's comfortable being herself, regardless of what people think.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark has the last word after DiJonai Carrington tries to rattle her
articles.standfirst: Clark stayed composed when things threatened to get heated
articles.summary: Clark stayed composed when things threatened to get heated
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark was put to the test by DiJonai Carrington during the Indiana Fever’s matchup against the Chicago Sky. Both players have been at the center of attention recently, and with them facing each other, Clark made it clear which side had the upper hand.

Carrington and the Fever already had some history this season following the Sophie Cunningham incident and Carrington’s subsequent viral social media post. The post came after Carrington was ejected for a Flagrant 2 foul on Cunningham, which she said was not intentional. Carrington later explained that her viral post was not in response to the foul call.

All eyes were on what could happen when the two teams met again

After the incident, there was plenty of attention on the game and what could unfold, with Carrington taking the initiative by trying to provoke Clark, who is known for having a short fuse.

However, Clark chose to remain calm and ignore the potential provocation , showing that she could keep her mind on the game instead of getting pulled into an opponent’s game. It came shortly after a viral moment involving Paige Bueckers, when the Dallas Wings star told Clark to calm down . This time, Clark appeared to follow that advice and stayed composed after Carrington made a seemingly unfriendly bump.

The moment came in the second quarter after Clark drilled a 3-pointer with Carrington in coverage. During the transition, Carrington bumped into Clark, but Clark quickly waved her off and did not let the brief encounter turn into anything more.

Clark had little reason to get caught up in the exchange

Instead, she let the moment pass and kept her attention on the game, especially with many expecting the situation to escalate. Clark finished with 37 points, a career-high eight 3-pointers and 10 assists, while her performance helped Indiana secure the win .

The result also eliminated Chicago from playoff contention after Sunday’s home loss to Indiana. Clark did not need to answer Carrington with another confrontation. Her performance had already done the talking.

articles.title: How Angel Reese broke two Historic WNBA rebounding records in one night
articles.standfirst: Angel Reese made WNBA history in a night she will never forget.
articles.summary: Angel Reese made WNBA history in a night she will never forget.
articles.body:
A ngel Reese broke the WNBA single-game rebounding record with 26 while also breaking the league's season record for rebounds as the Atlanta Dream beat the Los Angeles Sparks 78-71 on Monday night.

Reese surpassed Chamique Holdsclaw 's record of 24 rebounds , set on May 23, 2003 for Washington .

The Dream star has 458 rebounds this season, seven more than A'ja Wilson's mark set in 2024.

Reese finished with 11 points . She secured her WNBA-leading 27th double-double of the season on a basket with 13.9 seconds left in the game.

The Dream have beaten the Sparks nine straight times.

Allisha Gray led Atlanta (25-13) with 20 points. Rhyne Howard added 18 points to eclipse 3,000 for her career. Gray set an Atlanta record for field goals in a season with 247.

Nneka Ogwumike had 27 points and 16 rebounds for Los Angeles (13-25). Dearica Hamby and Cameron Brink each scored 15 points.

articles.title: Stephanie White rewards Caitlin Clark and teammates after the WNBA “wore down” the Indiana Fever
articles.standfirst: The Indiana locker room erupted after the team finally earned a badly needed break
articles.summary: The Indiana locker room erupted after the team finally earned a badly needed break
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever had just finished one of the most demanding stretches on their schedule when Stephanie White delivered the kind of postgame announcement every exhausted team wants to hear.

Moments after Indiana closed a five-game road trip with a 113-90 win over the Chicago Sky , White told her players they would have the next two days off.

The locker room response was immediate, with Caitlin Clark jumping out of her seat and celebrating alongside teammates. The timing made sense.

Indiana had played six games in 10 days, including five away from home, and Sunday’s matchup came less than 24 hours after a 109-102 loss to the New York Liberty .

The Fever responded with one of their strongest offensive performances of the trip, led by Clark ’s 37 points and Kelsey Mitchell ’s 30. That made the two-day break feel less like a reward and more like a necessary reset.

White knows when team needs a break

White has spoken openly about the strain of a WNBA season and the importance of leaning on the people around her when energy runs low.

“The reality is just like players: there are some days where it's like you just don't have it,” White said before the Liberty game. “Like, you just don't have it. Like, life happens. On those days, I can go to them, and I can say, 'Y'all, I need you today.'”

She also emphasized that leadership doesn't always mean carrying everything alone.

“And I think when you learn in life as we get older, we learn different things that we're not always leading from the front,” White added. “This is one thing we talked about with our team all the time.”

That message has been central to how she has handled a season filled with travel, injuries, pressure and outside noise.

Clark and teammates become part of White’s support system

White has also credited her players with helping her through difficult moments, saying the relationship works both ways.

“Sometimes you need somebody to lift you up,” she said. “Sometimes you need to lift somebody else up.”

She added: “I mean, look, these players are really incredible, like the way that they're able to minimize the outside noise. The way they're able to show up for each other and for me every day, [and] they lift me up.”

Sunday’s celebration was a lighter example of that connection.

The Fever now have four days before hosting the Connecticut Sun at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Friday, giving Clark , Mitchell and the rest of the roster a rare chance to recover before the next stretch begins.

Indiana needed the win in Chicago. Judging by Clark’s reaction, the players may have appreciated White’s next announcement just as much.

articles.title: The WNBA is in an uproar: Enes Kanter's plans with the Indiana Fever could send everything into a tailspin
articles.standfirst: Former NBA center says he intends to attend every Fever playoff game after his controversial ejection from the Chicago Sky matchup
articles.summary: Former NBA center says he intends to attend every Fever playoff game after his controversial ejection from the Chicago Sky matchup
articles.body:
E nes Kanter Freedom has no intention of disappearing from the WNBA spotlight after being ejected from Sunday's Indiana Fever-Chicago Sky game.

The former NBA center was removed from Wintrust Arena following a heated confrontation with Sky guard Natasha Cloud during the third quarter.

Now, rather than stepping away from the league, Kanter says he plans to attend every playoff game played by the Fever , potentially ensuring that the controversy surrounding him follows Indiana into the postseason.

Speaking with Fox News host Laura Ingraham after the incident, Kanter made his intentions clear.

"I am so excited for the playoffs," Kanter said. "I cannot wait to go to every playoff game that the Indiana Fever plays. It's going to be fun."

Kanter's comments come as the Fever enter the final stretch of the regular season in a strong position. Indiana is 25-14 with five regular-season games remaining and has already secured a playoff berth.

The team has also been one of the WNBA's biggest stories throughout the season, with Caitlin Clark 's return to action and the ongoing attention surrounding the franchise helping make its games among the league's most watched.

That means Kanter's planned presence could attract considerable attention.

When asked whether he expected to have difficulty obtaining tickets after his removal from the Chicago game, Kanter explained that he was taking precautions.

"I don't get those tickets under my name, because I don't know if they are going to cancel at the last minute or not. So, I'm getting those tickets under my manager's name,” he said.

The controversy goes beyond one courtside confrontation

Kanter's relationship with the WNBA has become increasingly controversial since he announced his intention to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft.

The former NBA player has argued that the league's rules leave room for his declaration, while the WNBA has not publicly provided a detailed policy addressing transgender eligibility.

However, that situation changed somewhat this week after multiple reports indicated that Kanter and former NBA player Royce White would not be eligible for the draft.

Reuters reported that sources around the league had confirmed their ineligibility, although the WNBA itself had not publicly announced the decision.

The league's collective bargaining agreement states that “only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA,” but it does not publicly spell out more detailed criteria regarding gender identity or sex assigned at birth.

That unresolved debate has placed Kanter at the center of a much wider argument.

His presence at the Fever-Sky game intensified matters. Kanter was sitting courtside wearing a shirt that read “WOMAN noun. adult human female.” Cloud approached him after scoring a basket, and security ultimately intervened as the confrontation escalated.

Cloud did not address the confrontation during her postgame media availability. She later posted a message supporting transgender people, writing that members of the transgender community belong to her community and should feel protected.

Kanter has meanwhile continued to align himself with Fever player Sophie Cunningham, whose comments about transgender athletes in women's sports have made her a prominent figure in the debate.

For Indiana, the priority remains basketball. The Fever are attempting to build momentum heading into the postseason, and their 113-90 victory over Chicago on Sunday further strengthened their position while eliminating the Sky from playoff contention.

Yet if Kanter follows through on his plan to attend Indiana's playoff games, the franchise could find itself sharing headlines with a controversy that has little to do with what happens on the court.

Kanter's stated intention is not simply to return to the WNBA. It is to remain visible around one of its most prominent teams at a time when the league is already grappling with an increasingly heated debate over gender, inclusion and eligibility.

Whether he is allowed to attend those games without further incident remains to be seen. But after Sunday's confrontation, Kanter has made one thing unmistakable: he does not plan to leave the WNBA conversation quietly.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham wanted to stay out of trouble after an unexpected request from a reporter
articles.standfirst: One request was enough for Sophie Cunningham to make it clear she wanted no part of it
articles.summary: One request was enough for Sophie Cunningham to make it clear she wanted no part of it
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham has quickly become a notable figure in the WNBA , not only because of the passion she brings to the court, but also because of how she gets into her opponents' heads during games. Her personality and outspoken nature have sparked conversations both on and off the court, making her one of the league's most controversial, followed and provoked players.

Her comments on transgender players in the WNBA have also brought plenty of attention, with many people accusing her of transphobia . At the same time, moments that once stood out for the way she provoked opponents, such as her famous pointing finger, have become viral.

The pointing finger became bigger than the moment itself

Those moments throughout the season have brought Cunningham plenty of attention, perhaps more than she expected or even wanted. The gesture, in particular, became so famous that fans have continued asking her to recreate it , including at her own youth basketball camp, where kids used the signature point while taking pictures with her .

It all started during a June game against Phoenix, when Cunningham silently pointed at DeWanna Bonner for 22 straight seconds during a heated exchange . The bizarre moment quickly exploded online and became one of the year's biggest WNBA memes.

But not every request is getting a yes

Now, as Cunningham left a building ahead of her game against the Indiana Fever, someone who appeared to be a photographer shouted for her to do the famous pointing gesture . The request was loud and clear, but Cunningham completely ignored it and didn't even turn toward the paparazzi waiting outside .

Apparently, Cunningham is willing to do the point for her young fans. Paparazzi, however, don't seem to be getting the same treatment. After everything that has surrounded her in recent weeks, it is possible Cunningham simply wants to stay away from the controversy, or she may have just decided to ignore a bizarre request from someone looking for a photo . Either way, safe to say she made the right call by not paying attention to the random request.

articles.title: Martina Navratilova defends Enes Kanter Freedom after his ejection: “It’s shameful… Is ‘woman’ now a dirty word?”
articles.standfirst: Tennis legend weighs in after heated WNBA confrontation as debate over gender eligibility intensifies
articles.summary: Tennis legend weighs in after heated WNBA confrontation as debate over gender eligibility intensifies
articles.body:
M artina Navratilova has entered the growing controversy surrounding Enes Kanter Freedom ’s ejection from a WNBA game, questioning the reaction to the former NBA player after his confrontation with Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud .

Freedom was removed from Wintrust Arena during Sunday’s Indiana Fever-Chicago Sky matchup after an increasingly heated exchange with Cloud late in the third quarter.

The former NBA center had been sitting courtside wearing a black shirt featuring the words “WOMAN noun. adult human female,” amid his increasingly vocal criticism of transgender participation in women’s sports.

According to footage from the incident, Cloud approached Freedom after scoring a basket and began pointing and shouting in his direction.

Freedom stood up and moved toward the court before security personnel and several Sky players intervened. He was subsequently escorted from the arena.

The incident quickly became another flashpoint in a debate that has moved beyond the basketball court. Navratilova , one of the most prominent athletes to speak publicly about transgender participation in women's sports, reacted to the situation on social media.

“Disgraceful- woman is apparently a bad word now???” Navratilova wrote.

Her intervention adds another high-profile voice to a dispute that has already drawn players, former athletes, politicians and commentators into opposing camps.

Navratilova’s stance adds another layer to the WNBA dispute

Navratilova has previously argued that protecting women's competitive opportunities and maintaining separate women's sporting categories are important.

Her latest comments come as the WNBA finds itself dealing with an increasingly public argument over transgender participation.

Freedom has deliberately placed himself at the center of that discussion. Earlier this month, he announced plans to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft, presenting his move as a challenge to the league's approach to eligibility.

Former NBA player Royce White has made a similar declaration. However, reports from Reuters said sources had determined that the pair would not be eligible to participate in the draft.

Freedom has disputed reports that he has been ruled ineligible, calling them “fake news” and saying he had not received direct communication from the WNBA.

His appearance at the Fever-Sky game therefore carried an obvious political and cultural dimension.

The shirt he wore was particularly notable given the circumstances, while his public support for Indiana player Sophie Cunningham has also connected him to the wider argument over gender eligibility.

The confrontation with Cloud intensified the situation. Cloud did not address reporters after the game, but later posted a message supporting the transgender community. Her statement said trans people belong, are loved and should be protected.

Sky coach Tyler Marsh subsequently defended Cloud, saying she was someone who protects her team and people who need protection. He also urged fans to attend games to enjoy the basketball.

The game itself ultimately became secondary to the controversy. Indiana won 113-90, with Caitlin Clark scoring 37 points and Kelsey Mitchell adding 30, while Chicago's defeat eliminated the Sky from playoff contention.

For Navratilova , however, the argument represents something larger than one courtside confrontation. Her response shows how strongly she believes language surrounding women and women's sport should remain part of the public conversation.

The episode also illustrates the difficult position the WNBA now faces. Questions about gender eligibility, inclusion and competitive fairness are increasingly being discussed alongside games themselves, while league officials attempt to navigate a politically charged subject.

Freedom's ejection, Navratilova's reaction and Cloud's subsequent message have ensured that the debate will continue long after the final score in Chicago.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers puts the WNBA on notice as the Wings move one win away from the playoffs
articles.standfirst: This season, Bueckers leads the Wings in minutes, points, and assists as she aim for her first playoff appearance
articles.summary: This season, Bueckers leads the Wings in minutes, points, and assists as she aim for her first playoff appearance
articles.body:
Following the games this upcoming Sunday, the WNBA will halt play from August 31 through September 16, to accommodate the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, Germany.

During this international showcase, 12 WNBA stars, including Caitlin Clark , A'ja Wilson , Paige Bueckers , and Breanna Stewart , will represent their countries in Group D, facing China on September 4th, Italy on September 6th, and Czechia on September 7th.

This week there is still plenty of action, including today's crucial matchup between the Dallas Wings and the Portland Fire . With seven teams already qualified for the postseason , these two squads are battling for the eighth and final playoff spot, but the Wings hold a commanding edge as a victory tonight will officially secure their ticket for the first time since 2023 .

Paige Bueckers Shines as Dallas Nears Playoff Berth

If they stumble today, Dallas sits on a comfortable cushion, holding a 6.5-game advantage over the expansion Portland franchise with just a handful of games remaining. After bottoming out with the league's worst record last year, the Wings have completely flipped the script.

Spearheaded by reigning Rookie of the Year Paige Bueckers and elite rebounding from Jessica Shepard , the squad recently matched a single-season franchise record with 22 wins following a dominant 92-70 rout of the Seattle Storm on Sunday, securing their first back-to-back victories in over a month.

Bueckers put on an absolute clinic against Seattle, exploding for a game-high 32 points while shooting a flawless 6-of-6 from beyond the arc (a new career high) across just 26 minutes of action, getting the luxury of sitting out the entire fourth quarter. She poured in 18 points in the opening frame alone, tying the franchise record for the most productive first quarter in Wings history.

An Uncompromising Competitive Edge and International Aspirations

Following that stellar performance, Bueckers delivered a blunt message to reporters that encapsulated her relentless drive: "Losing sucks. I friggin hate losing." That fierce competitive fire has defined her time in the professional ranks, especially after she carried an immense load following a tough debut team campaign.

Statistically, Bueckers anchors Dallas across the board, pacing the roster in minutes (33.3) , points (20.6 per game) , and assists (5.8 per game) . With teammate Azzi Fudd sidelined for the remainder of the year due to knee surgery, Bueckers has stepped up her defensive intensity to help fill the void.

Her development will only accelerate in Germany during the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup , where she will battle elite guards like Caitlin Clark , Jackie Young , Chelsea Gray , and Rhyne Howard for valuable starting minutes.

Once tonight's showdown with Portland concludes, the Wings will wrap up their pre-break schedule against the Connecticut Sun on Sunday, looking to lock down momentum before the global stage takes center stage.

articles.title: Angel Reese shuts down reporter after WNBA slip up
articles.standfirst: Reese made it clear she will not let anyone undermine the WNBA or what she has accomplished
articles.summary: Reese made it clear she will not let anyone undermine the WNBA or what she has accomplished
articles.body:
A ngel Reese considers herself one of the most important faces of the WNBA and is willing to give the league the recognition she believes it deserves. After an awkward moment with a reporter in the media room, it became clear that Reese was not going to tolerate a mistake that could be seen as dismissive of the league, its players or her accomplishments .

For some, the reporter’s use of “NBA” instead of “WNBA” was a genuine mistake . For others, the issue was not the mistake itself, but t he way he tried to fix the situation after being corrected . Reese, however, kept control of the moment and made it clear who was in charge of the interview.

Reese was not letting the moment slide

The exchange happened after Reese helped the Atlanta Dream defeat the Los Angeles Sparks 78-71. A reporter congratulated her on an “NBA record” after she had just broken two WNBA rebounding records . When the mistake was addressed, the reporter tried to play it off, telling Reese she knew what he meant. Reese pushed back, pointing out that she also sets NBA records, before the reporter tried to smooth things over by saying that was exactly what he meant.

Some felt Reese went too far with her response, while others believed it was the right way to make the distinction clear . The WNBA is a women’s league, but that does not make its records or accomplishments less important than those in the NBA.

Two records, one historic night

Reese continues to break records, and while some may make fun of which records she is breaking or how she is surpassing them, she continues to embrace them. She knows her presence with the Dream and across the WNBA is making a difference, and no one will take away the accomplishments she has earned in her third professional season.

The exchange came after a historic performance in which Reese grabbed 26 rebounds , breaking Chamique Holdsclaw’s WNBA record of 24, set in 2003 with Washington. She also reached 458 rebounds on the season, surpassing A’ja Wilson’s 2024 mark of 451 to set a new WNBA single-season record.

Her response ultimately shifted the attention back to the WNBA and her record-breaking performance, making sure the league received the recognition it deserved.

articles.title: WNBA team bans Enes Kanter Freedom after explosive ccourtside clash with Natasha Cloud
articles.standfirst: The Chicago Sky have taken action and banned the former NBA player from returning to their arena.
articles.summary: The Chicago Sky have taken action and banned the former NBA player from returning to their arena.
articles.body:
Former NBA player Enes Kanter Freedom , who has become one of the most controversial figures in the debate surrounding the WNBA ’s policies regarding transgender athletes, was removed from Wintrust Arena after an exchange with Chicago Sky star Natasha Cloud during Sunday’s game against the Indiana Fever.

Freedom was escorted out of the arena and, according to Sky owner Michael Alter , the former New York Knicks player will not be allowed to return “unless sometime in the future he is able to prove to us that he can abide by our rules without becoming a potential threat.”

Alter said Freedom’s presence at the game against the Indiana Fever appeared to be aimed at creating controversy and attracting attention.

“It was pretty clear to us that his purpose of coming here was trying to be provocative and just see how much attention he could get,” Alter told Front Office Sports, adding that he knew Kanter was going to attend the game but did not want to alert his players beforehand.

Freedom attended the game wearing a shirt that read: “WOMAN noun. adult human female” and said he was simply supporting Indiana player Sophie Cunningham , who had sparked debate after speaking about transgender athletes competing in women’s sports.

However, Alter said the incident went beyond the message on Freedom’s shirt and claimed that Kanter was the one who initiated the exchange with Cloud.

“They each confirmed that the dialogue between Cloud and Kanter started with Kanter,” Alter told FOS. “He began to chirp with her sometime in the third quarter. I would characterize it as trash-talking, nothing personal. Basketball-related, but enough to get her attention and to engage her, and in my opinion, to try to provoke her.”

“He portrays himself as this victimless person who did nothing, said nothing. Just wearing a T-shirt… We have five different security authorities that all agreed very quickly to throw him out because he made himself into a threat.”

The Sky owner added that Freedom attempted to portray himself as someone who “did nothing and said nothing,” but that five security teams quickly agreed he needed to be removed because they considered him a potential threat.

The controversy involving Freedom and the WNBA grew after he and former Houston Rockets first-round pick Royce White entered the league’s debate over transgender policies by declaring themselves women and seeking eligibility for the WNBA Draft .

“I haven’t heard anything from the WNBA officials yet,” he told The Post’s Stefan Bondy. “Fake News!”

Alter said Freedom’s presence at the game against the Indiana Fever appeared to be aimed at creating controversy and attracting attention.

“It was pretty clear to us that his purpose of coming here was trying to be provocative and just see how much attention he could get,” Alter told Front Office Sports, adding that he knew Kanter was going to attend the game but did not want to alert his players beforehand.

Freedom attended the game wearing a shirt that read: “WOMAN noun. adult human female” and said he was simply supporting Indiana player Sophie Cunningham , who had sparked debate after speaking about transgender athletes competing in women’s sports.
However, Alter said the incident went beyond the message on Freedom’s shirt and claimed that Kanter was the one who initiated the exchange with Cloud.

“They each confirmed that the dialogue between Cloud and Kanter started with Kanter,” Alter told FOS. “He began to chirp with her sometime in the third quarter. I would characterize it as trash-talking, nothing personal. Basketball-related, but enough to get her attention and to engage her, and in my opinion, to try to provoke her.”

“He portrays himself as this victimless person who did nothing, said nothing. Just wearing a T-shirt… We have five different security authorities that all agreed very quickly to throw him out because he made himself into a threat.”

The Sky owner added that Freedom attempted to portray himself as someone who “did nothing and said nothing,” but that five security teams quickly agreed he needed to be removed because they considered him a potential threat.

The controversy involving Freedom and the WNBA grew after he and former Houston Rockets first-round pick Royce White entered the league’s debate over transgender policies by declaring themselves women and seeking eligibility for the WNBA Draft .

“I haven’t heard anything from the WNBA officials yet,” he told The Post’s Stefan Bondy. “Fake News!”
