articles.title: Charles Barkley reveals the real reason the WNBA hates Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham
articles.standfirst: Charles Barkley enters the WNBA controversy and reveals what he believes is fueling the tension surrounding Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham.
articles.summary: Charles Barkley enters the WNBA controversy and reveals what he believes is fueling the tension surrounding Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham.
articles.body:
Charles Barkley has finally weighed in on the controversy surrounding the WNBA , saying that the tension surrounding the league’s biggest stars, Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham , stems from a combination of factors, including jealousy, race, and sexuality.

During an appearance on Michael Smerconish ’s show, the longtime Inside the NBA analyst reiterated that he believes much of the criticism directed at Clark within the league has been unfair. However, this time he partially agreed with his well-known “rival” Jason Whitlock , acknowledging that several elements influence how Clark and Cunningham are perceived by some players and members of the WNBA community.

Smerconish brought up a previous segment on his CNN program featuring J ason Whitlock and Cari Champion , in which Whitlock argued that the league’s internal tensions are connected to sexual identity and a kind of “closing ranks” among players. Barkley offered his own perspective on the situation.

“I think there’s some, like I say, it’s jealousy, I think it’s a part of it. Race is a part of it, and sexuality is a part of it. Now, I don’t know how much, but I’m comfortable saying they don’t like Caitlin. I have no idea why. She’s just a really good basketball player. Same thing with Sophie. She’s a good player, but I think it has something to do with sexuality, race, and jealousy. I think it’s all three of them. I don’t know how you break up the percentages,” Barkley said.

Barkley’s comments come after the former NBA star publicly supported a petition calling for clearer eligibility rules within the WNBA.

Although Barkley and Whitlock often disagree, the two remain friends. Barkley described their relationship as direct and without filters, while also calling Whitlock’s comments “provocative.”

Still, he referenced Whitlock’s argument again by stating:

“There is something going on with those women.”

The discussion gained momentum after the incident between DiJonai Carrington and Sophie Cunningham, in which Carrington was assessed a Flagrant 2 foul . Carrington’s subsequent comments in the locker room sparked widespread reaction and even brought Caitlin Clark into the conversation, fueling debate over whether the rivalry in the WNBA is driven solely by basketball-related issues.

Smerconish’s program highlighted two completely opposing views regarding the root causes of the league’s tensions.

Whitlock argued that sexual identity is one of the main factors behind the animosity toward players like Clark and Cunningham. He also pointed to race and competitive jealousy, while citing comments from veterans such as Syd Colson and Monica McNutt , who have called for Clark to “join the sisterhood,” as a possible sign of an exclusionary culture.

Meanwhile, Cari Champion strongly rejected that interpretation, calling the focus on sexuality an “easy” and “ridiculous” argument. She acknowledged that race can play a role but argued that outside commentators have amplified the conflict.

“That has nothing to do with why these women don’t like Caitlin Clark or Sophie Cunningham,” Champion said, emphasizing that physical play is simply part of basketball.

“It’s a contact sport. They’re going to touch each other. It happens in the NBA, it’s going to happen in the WNBA.”

Barkley said he watched that discussion and agreed with several of Champion’s points, although he admitted he could not completely dismiss Whitlock’s perspective.

As opinions remain divided, Barkley’s stance represents a middle ground: he believes the tension within the WNBA cannot be explained by a single factor and that multiple issues have contributed to the conflict as the league experiences unprecedented growth in popularity and media attention.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark opens up on the harsh reality of success and the hate that comes with it
articles.standfirst: Her mother's warning that "people want to see you fail" feels very different after everything the Fever star has experienced in the spotlight
articles.summary: Her mother's warning that "people want to see you fail" feels very different after everything the Fever star has experienced in the spotlight
articles.body:
C aitlin Clark has heard the cheers of packed arenas and watched women's basketball reach audiences few imagined possible only a few years ago. But she has also discovered that becoming one of the most recognizable athletes in America means experiencing the other side of that attention just as intensely.

The Indiana Fever star has been knocked to the floor, caught by hard fouls and found herself at the center of confrontations that sometimes explode into national debates. One particularly frightening moment saw Clark take a blow around the neck and head area, another physical play added to a growing collection of clips dissected frame by frame.

Every incident seems to produce two competing versions of the same story: those who believe opponents are targeting her and those who accuse Clark of receiving special treatment because of her enormous popularity.

And the criticism hasn't stopped when the whistle blows. Her reactions, complaints to officials, body language and relationships with other players have all been scrutinized.

When she succeeds, she's credited with transforming the women's game. When something goes wrong, there is another group waiting to question whether the attention surrounding her was ever deserved.

Caitlin Clark was warned that success would come with hate

That makes something Clark once revealed during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show feel almost prophetic. Speaking with McAfee about the enormous attention and criticism surrounding her rise, Clark recalled a brutally simple warning her mother, Anne, had given her growing up: "People want to see you fail."

"That's just kind of how our world is, which is really sad," Clark said. She also revealed one of the best pieces of advice she received about dealing with the extremes that accompany success: "At the level you feel all the praise, that's the same level you'll feel all the hate." Her solution has been to try to live somewhere between them. "I try to stay right in the middle."

It sounds simple until considering what that middle now looks like. Clark has become a player capable of generating enormous television audiences and sold-out arenas while simultaneously becoming a lightning rod for arguments about everything from officiating and physicality to race , popularity and the direction of the WNBA .

Even people who don't watch every Fever game seem to have an opinion about her.

Yet Clark's response to all of that remains remarkably uncomplicated. "I don't really think about that type of stuff," she said. "I just go out there and do me."

Years later, those words carry considerably more weight. Her mother warned her that people would eventually want to see her fail. What neither of them could have known was just how many people would be watching when they got the chance.

articles.title: “Caitlin Clark is like Steph Curry, but with Michael Jordan's mindset”
articles.standfirst: The Fever star has kept focus on basketball while controversy continues to swirl around the league
articles.summary: The Fever star has kept focus on basketball while controversy continues to swirl around the league
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark has no shortage of reasons to dominate the conversation around the WNBA . Her latest record-setting performance only added to that, but it is the way she has handled the noise around the league that has caught Colin Cowherd ’s attention.

The Indiana Fever star became the first player in WNBA history to post five career games with at least 30 points and 10 assists on August 23, another landmark in a rapidly growing resume.

Yet Cowherd believes Clark ’s most striking trait isn't simply her range or playmaking. It is her willingness to keep the public focus on basketball.

“She is Steph Curry but with a Michael Jordan mindset,” Cowherd said on The Herd. “All business. All basketball. Has no opinion or comment on the controversies.”

He continued: “The Fever offense is not only number one in this league at 97 a game. It’s the best offense in league history because of Caitlin Clark.”

Cowherd sees Jordan-like traits

The comparison with Michael Jordan is less about style of play than public approach. Jordan spent much of his career avoiding being defined by political or social debates, a stance he later explained in a 2020 ESPN interview.

“I never thought of myself as an activist, I thought of myself as a basketball player,” Jordan said. “I wasn’t a politician when I was playing my sport; I was focused on my craft.”

Clark has taken a similarly narrow approach when asked about some of the WNBA’s most contentious issues.

Discussing the debate around transgender athletes in women’s sports earlier this month, she said: “I think it’s for leagues and governing bodies to work with their athletes to find solutions. Our focus is on basketball.”

She reinforced that message in another ESPN interview.

“I think first and foremost, like you know, you speak when you feel like you want to speak,” Clark said. “I try to just show up and be myself every single day.”

That position has drawn criticism from some who believe a player with Clark ’s platform should take stronger positions. Cowherd , however, sees restraint as part of what makes her so effective.

Tension around Clark goes deeper

The broader debate around Clark and teammate Sophie Cunningham has also drawn Charles Barkley into the conversation.

“Those girls do not like Caitlin Clark or Sophie Cunningham,” Barkley said on The Michael Smerconish Program.

He went on to suggest several possible factors behind the tension, though he stopped short of accusing anyone of racism.

“I’m not gonna get on here and call somebody a racist because I don’t have any proof,” Barkley said.

He added: “I think there’s some, like I say it, jealousy. I think it’s a part of it. Race is a part of it. And sexuality is a part of it.”

That contrast helps explain why Cowherd finds Clark ’s approach notable.

While others debate the controversies surrounding her, Clark keeps returning to the same message: basketball first.

And in Cowherd ’s view, that is exactly what makes the Curry-Jordan comparison work.

articles.title: Enes Kanter receives embarrassing advice from Jason Williams on how to qualify for the WNBA
articles.standfirst: Williams questioned Kanter’s motives after Wintrust Arena ejection
articles.summary: Williams questioned Kanter’s motives after Wintrust Arena ejection
articles.body:
Enes Kanter Freedom wanted to force a conversation around the WNBA . After his ejection from Wintrust Arena and the backlash that followed, that is exactly what happened, just not always in the way he may have intended.

Former NBA champion Jason Williams became the latest ex-player to weigh in after Freedom ’s heated exchange with Natasha Cloud , and his response was blunt.

Rather than debating the former center’s stated argument about eligibility rules, Williams questioned why he was seeking this kind of attention in the first place.

“Why does he want to play with women?” Williams said on the Hoopin’ N Hollerin’ podcast.

He continued: “Why does he need attention? Just do a podcast or some sh*t. Why the f**k do you want to play with girls? I don’t get that, dog. The last thing I want in life is attention. That’s the last thing.”

WNBA should let the stunt play out

Freedom has said he intends to declare for the 2027 WNBA Draft as part of his challenge to the league’s eligibility language.

The WNBA collective bargaining agreement states that “only players who are women are eligible to play in the WNBA,” and league sources have said Freedom is ineligible.

Still, Williams suggested the cleanest response might be to let the idea collapse on its own.

“That’s where he’s at in life. I mean, come on, dawg,” Williams said. “There’s no need for that. You know what I mean? Come on. What does that prove, dawg? I hope they let him enter the draft and nobody picks his a**.”

The criticism came after Freedom attended the Chicago Sky game against the Indiana Fever wearing a shirt that read, “WOMAN noun. adult human female.”

His interaction with Cloud escalated during the game, and security ultimately removed him from the arena.

Freedom became a security concern

The consequences extended beyond one ejection. Chicago Sky owner Michael Alter said Freedom had been indefinitely barred from home games, although he left open the possibility of reconsidering that decision in the future.

“The whole thing changed when he decided to get up,” Alter said.

He added: “The security’s job isn’t to wait to see how far they get before they do something. It’s to get there before that happens and avoid it.”

A league source said there would be no WNBA-wide ban. The broader criticism has also come from outside the league. Fox News personality Arthel Neville questioned whether Freedom ’s campaign was genuinely about supporting women’s sports.

“Why are we trying to intellectualize this publicity stunt? It’s pathetic. It’s ridiculous,” Neville said.

That's now the central divide around Freedom ’s campaign. Supporters see an attempt to provoke a policy discussion. Critics see an attention-seeking exercise built around confrontation.

Williams clearly falls in the second camp, and his proposed solution is simple: let the draft idea happen, then see what comes next.

articles.title: 'Joe Rogan Sphere' blamed for intensifying Sophie Cunningham controversy in debate over transgender WNBA players
articles.standfirst: The league remains under pressure as commentators clash over eligibility, free speech and the wider political climate
articles.summary: The league remains under pressure as commentators clash over eligibility, free speech and the wider political climate
articles.body:
The debate over transgender athletes in women’s sports has become one of the loudest issues surrounding the WNBA , and veteran MMA analyst Luke Thomas believes the conversation now extends far beyond basketball.

Speaking on his YouTube channel, Thomas addressed the criticism directed at Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham , who has publicly opposed transgender women competing in women’s sports.

He argued that reactions to her comments are being shaped by a much broader political and cultural climate.

“There’s an inherent contradiction though, that I think needs to be addressed a little bit,” Thomas said. “I don’t know if you’re asking why is Sophie getting a lot of pushback? Again, partly, it’s a culture war issue.”

His argument wasn't that Cunningham ’s comments themselves amounted to an attack on transgender people. Instead, Thomas said the issue has become tangled with a wider media ecosystem in which transgender issues are frequently discussed in combative terms.

Luke Thomas points to the ‘Rogan sphere’

Thomas referenced what comedian Marc Maron has described as the “Rogan sphere,” a loose network of commentators and personalities associated with or influenced by Joe Rogan ’s podcasting orbit.

“People are very, very sensitive right now to what it means to be speaking out against people who are, whose ability to have a public life at all is, frankly, being under assault,” Thomas said.

He added: “There’s this larger climate of, like, you know, Marc Maron was talking about this related to the Rogan sphere, where all these guys make a career on, you know, going after trans folks, not just trans athletes, but trans folks.”

Rogan has repeatedly argued that biological sex should determine eligibility in women’s sports and has called for the WNBA to use chromosomes as a defining standard.

“If you want to play in the WNBA, you have to have XX,” Rogan said on his podcast.

That position has drawn attention partly because there are currently no transgender women playing in the WNBA.

Cunningham remains at center of controversy

The debate accelerated after Cunningham addressed the subject in an ESPN interview.

“I think that I am here to extend love,” she said. “But I also think with that love is truth, being honest. And I want to protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn’t have to go against biological men.”

She later added: “I said what I said. I think it’s kind of common sense.”

Her remarks have since become part of a much larger dispute involving rallies outside Fever games, criticism of teammate Caitlin Clark ’s more neutral stance and publicity campaigns from former NBA players including Enes Kanter Freedom and Royce White .

Sportscaster Chris Williamson argued that the league should have acted against Cunningham , writing that “her conduct has objectively been detrimental to the league.”

The WNBA hasn't disciplined her. Instead, the league later issued a broader statement condemning “hate, abuse, and demonization” while saying it would continue difficult conversations without being used as a political pawn.

What began as one player’s opinion has therefore become something much larger, a clash over sports eligibility, free expression and the cultural environment surrounding transgender issues.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham's next WNBA team identified as Indiana Fever exit gains steam
articles.standfirst: The divisive Cunningham could have a future at a different destination next season.
articles.summary: The divisive Cunningham could have a future at a different destination next season.
articles.body:
Even before the 2026 WNBA season , Sophie Cunningham had become one of the most talked about players in the league. She turned that into a major podcast deal midway through last season.

But 2026 has been a whole other story. Her comments on transgender athletes sparked outrage among many , and it has put a target on her back over the past month and change. That national spotlight could very well lead to Cunningham landing with a new team next season.

She signed a one-year deal in the offseason to stay with the Indiana Fever . So far this season, she has played her role as a spark off the bench, but the team probably doesn't want the constant spotlight, especially when it's overly negative.

Sophie Cunningham expected to leave Indiana Fever in the offseason

With the idea of Cunningham leaving, Sportskeeda got to work on identifying the top five landing spots for the 30-year-old veteran. Coming in at No. 1 are the New York Liberty .

Sophie Cunningham to the New York Liberty is a possibility, as they are not afraid to make bold moves. The Liberty made a splash last offseason by signing three-time WNBA All-Star Satou Sabally to an already loaded team that includes Breanna Stewart, Sabrina Ionescu and Jonquel Jones. However, Sabally has played in just 10 games so far due to lingering injury issues. Cunningham could be New York's occasional starter and a key contributor off the bench.

While the Liberty are the top potential destination, four other teams were also linked that make sense: Minnesota Lynx , Washington Mystics , Dallas Wings , and Phoenix Mercury .

Set to be an unrestricted free agent next offseason, Cunningham will have plenty of options to choose from. Returning to the Fever might not be one of them.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and Fever take Chicago Sky rivalry to TV heights unseen in 29 years without Angel Reese
articles.standfirst: For years Clark vs. Reese was considered the heartbeat of Fever-Sky, but 3.31 million viewers just sent a very different message
articles.summary: For years Clark vs. Reese was considered the heartbeat of Fever-Sky, but 3.31 million viewers just sent a very different message
articles.body:
For years, it was almost impossible to separate Caitlin Clark from Angel Reese whenever the Indiana Fever and Chicago Sky met. Their rivalry followed them from college into the WNBA , turning games between two rebuilding franchises into must-see television. Then Reese left Chicago, and there was an obvious question: would people still care quite as much?

Sunday night provided a remarkable answer. Fever-Sky averaged 3.31 million viewers across NBC and Peacock and peaked at 3.82 million , making it the most-watched WNBA regular-season game since the league's opening weekend in 1997.

Only two regular-season games in WNBA history have drawn larger audiences: New York Liberty-Los Angeles Sparks with 5.04 million on June 21, 1997, and Charlotte Sting-Phoenix Mercury with 3.59 million one day later. Twenty-nine years and thousands of WNBA games passed before anyone came this close again.

And Clark gave those millions a reason to keep watching. She exploded for 37 points and 10 assists, buried a career-high eight three-pointers and helped Indiana crush Chicago 113-90. Kelsey Mitchell poured in another 30 points as the Fever hit a franchise-record 18 threes.

Clark and Mitchell have now produced three games in which both scored at least 30 points , another WNBA record.

Caitlin Clark and Fever-Sky no longer need Angel Reese to fill the screen

What makes the number particularly striking is who wasn't there. Reese, whose battles with Clark helped turn Fever-Sky into one of the league's signature rivalries, was traded to the Atlanta Dream in April. But the emotion surrounding these teams didn't disappear with her.

This was their first meeting since DiJonai Carrington was ejected for a Flagrant 2 after taking down Sophie Cunningham on a breakaway on Aug. 8.

Yet the bigger story may now extend beyond Chicago altogether. Indiana has been involved in four of the 10 most-watched regular-season games in WNBA history , all this season: Sunday's 3.31 million against Chicago, 2.64 million against Las Vegas, 2.60 million against Atlanta and 2.50 million against Minnesota.

The Fever have also set viewing records this season on CBS, ESPN and Amazon Prime Video . Different opponents, different storylines, but the same team and the same No. 22 at the center of it.

For a rivalry that became famous because Clark and Reese seemed destined to be linked forever, perhaps Sunday's audience revealed something neither the Fever nor the WNBA could have known when it began . Angel Reese was no longer wearing a Sky uniform and there was no Clark-Reese showdown to sell, yet 3.82 million people were watching at the game's peak.

Fever-Sky may have started as a rivalry between two stars, but Caitlin Clark and Indiana are beginning to look like a television event all by themselves.

articles.title: Angel Reese turned mockery into fuel and now has a new record
articles.standfirst: Atlanta Dream’s star broke two rebounding records in a single night, while answering on the court those who for months questioned her style of play and even labeled her rebounds as “mebounds.”
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream’s star broke two rebounding records in a single night, while answering on the court those who for months questioned her style of play and even labeled her rebounds as “mebounds.”
articles.body:
A ngel Reese is going through the best moment of her career just when the noise surrounding her figure seemed hardest to ignore. The Atlanta Dream player has just set two WNBA rebounding records in a single night and is turning the criticism she received for months into one of the main sources of motivation behind her transformation.

On Monday, against the Los Angeles Sparks , Reese grabbed 26 rebounds in Atlanta's 78-71 victory. The total not only surpassed the record of 24 that Chamique Holdscla w had set in 2003, but it also brought Reese to 458 rebounds on the season, seven more than the previous record held by A"ja Wilson.

The word that was born as mockery and ended up working in her favor

For months, some social media users accused Reese of chasing rebounds to pad her stats, especially after misses near the rim. That is how the term “mebounds” emerged, a derogatory way of referring to the rebounds she supposedly grabbed after her own missed shots.

But Reese decided to turn the situation around. The player even applied to register “mebounds” to turn it into a brand and floated the idea of using it on products whose profits would be intended to combat cyberbullying. Instead of trying to silence her critics, she found a way to turn their own mockery into part of her narrative.

From criticism to records

What stands out most is that her response is not being limited to social media. In recent weeks, Reese has shown clear progress in her game. Before her record-setting night, she had posted 31 points and 14 rebounds against Phoenix and had also delivered a perfect game in which she made all nine of her field goal attempts against Los Angeles.

Her production this season reflects that growth: she is setting personal highs in scoring and minutes, while increasing her confidence to handle the ball, shoot from outside, and contest shots. Atlanta coach Karl Smesko emphasized that the player has been improving practically month by month.

And there is still room for her record to become even harder to reach. Reese reached 458 rebounds with six regular-season games still left to play. In addition, her 27 double-doubles left her just one shy of Alyssa Thomas's single-season record.

The transformation also has a personal component. Reese has endured constant criticism, racist and sexist attacks, and enormous pressure since her college days, when her rivalry with Caitlin Clark became one of the biggest focal points in women’s basketball. Now, while detractors keep looking for her mistakes, her numbers tell another story: Angel is no longer just surviving the noise; she is using that noise as fuel to become one of the most decisive figures in the WNBA.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark’s new Nike sneakers seemingly inspired by Taylor Swift’s iconic friendship bracelets
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark revealed a new pair of Nike sneakers on her Instagram Stories, and fans immediately noticed what appeared to be a nod to one of her biggest idols, Taylor Swift.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark revealed a new pair of Nike sneakers on her Instagram Stories, and fans immediately noticed what appeared to be a nod to one of her biggest idols, Taylor Swift.

In collaboration with Nike, Clark debuted a design that seems to reference the friendship bracelets made famous by Swift’s Eras Tour.

While the connection has not been confirmed, the resemblance was hard to miss, especially considering Clark is one of the singer’s biggest fans.

The sneakers feature Clark’s two “CC” initials on one side and the number 22 on the other, decorated with charms reminiscent of those found on friendship bracelets.

The laces also feature colorful charms, while the mostly white sneakers include pastel-colored, tie-dye-inspired details. Whether intentional or not, the design feels like a clear Swiftie touch and a major win for both Clark and Nike.

articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom's proposal to WNBA involves Caitlyn Jenner: “I'm offering a peace deal”
articles.standfirst: After his Chicago ban, Freedom says he wants a sit-down with league officials rather than another public clash
articles.summary: After his Chicago ban, Freedom says he wants a sit-down with league officials rather than another public clash
articles.body:
Enes Kanter Freedom has spent weeks pushing the WNBA into an uncomfortable debate over transgender eligibility. Now, after an ejection in Chicago and an arena ban, he says he wants to change the setting entirely.

Rather than another courtside confrontation, Freedom is proposing what he calls a “peace summit” with league leadership, with Caitlyn Jenner serving as moderator.

The former NBA center laid out the idea in an interview with Benny Johnson , saying he would be willing to sit down with WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert and other league officials if they were open to it.

“I think if, you know, if the NBA and the task force, and obviously, the commissioner, Cathy Engelbert, are okay with it, I am offering them a peace summit that is moderated by one of the best female athletes ever, Caitlyn Jenner,” Freedom said.

“I think she’ll be the best person to understand what’s going on and moderate the whole thing.”

Jenner has already agreed to help

According to Freedom, the proposal isn't purely hypothetical.

He said he had already spoken with Jenner , the 1976 Olympic decathlon champion who later came out as transgender, and claimed she was willing to get involved.

“I actually had a conversation with her last night,” Freedom said. “She said, ‘Listen, I love what you’re doing, just whatever you’re doing, just count me in. I will do anything to help it.’

“I was like, ‘Listen, we might offer them a peace summit. Would you be okay to moderate it?’ She said, ‘Amen.’”

Jenner has previously backed a biological-sex standard for women’s sports, saying the WNBA should adopt a simple rule: “XX, you’re in; XY, you’re out.”

There are currently no transgender women playing in the WNBA, but the issue has become a major flashpoint around the league.

Chicago incident still hangs over proposal

The timing of Freedom ’s offer is notable. He was recently removed from Wintrust Arena after a heated exchange involving Chicago Sky guard Natasha Cloud .

The Sky later banned him from home games, while the WNBA itself stopped short of imposing a league-wide ban.

That episode intensified criticism of Freedom , with some accusing him of deliberately seeking confrontation rather than policy discussion. He's now trying to present a different image.

“I’m a peacemaker,” Freedom said. “I don’t want to cause any trouble, you know? People obviously might get the wrong idea because of some of the things they might see on the internet.”

Whether the WNBA has any interest in accepting the proposed summit remains unclear. What has changed is Freedom ’s approach.

After weeks of public provocation and controversy, he's now pitching a formal discussion, with Jenner positioned as the person he believes could bridge the divide.

articles.title: Cameron Brink ruthlessly attacks Enes Kanter Freedom: “He's a stupid piece of s**t”
articles.standfirst: The Sparks star accused Freedom of chasing clicks and targeting a vulnerable community
articles.summary: The Sparks star accused Freedom of chasing clicks and targeting a vulnerable community
articles.body:
Cameron Brink didn't hedge when asked about Enes Kanter Freedom ’s increasingly public campaign around transgender eligibility in the WNBA .

Speaking after Los Angeles Sparks practice, Brink dismissed the issue as one being manufactured for attention and then delivered one of the strongest rebukes yet from an active player.

“For me personally, when it comes to the trans issues I believe you're talking about, I think it's a non-issue and it's people trying to just come for the trans community, and I just don't stand for that,” Brink told The Mirror US.

“I don't know what the f**k his name is, Enes Kanter, like he's a stupid piece of s**t.”

Her criticism arrived as Freedom continues to push the WNBA into a wider political and cultural debate despite there currently being no transgender women playing in the league.

Controversy is being manufactured

Brink ’s objection wasn't simply to Freedom ’s position. It was to the way she believes he is using the league to amplify it.

“I think people are tuned in [to the WNBA] for the right reasons,” Brink said. “It's great that we can all talk about things that are important and hard, and you can have your opinions on that.”

She added: “But I think taking something that's like a non-issue right now and trying to use it for clickbait, for views, for likes, and then targeting a vulnerable community is just really low.”

That stance is consistent with Brink ’s previous comments about inclusion in women’s basketball. She has spoken publicly about having teammates who use they/them pronouns and has argued that players shouldn't receive more attention simply because they fit a particular image.

“I want everyone to be accepted, not just paid attention to because of how they look,” Brink previously told UPROXX.

Chicago ejection added fuel to dispute

The latest backlash follows Freedom ’s appearance at Sunday’s Indiana Fever-Chicago Sky game, where he was escorted out of Wintrust Arena after a verbal exchange with Natasha Cloud .

According to Freedom , Cloud told him, “She's not going to sleep with you,” after he reacted to a Sophie Cunningham three-pointer.

He said he responded that he wasn't there “to sleep with her,” but instead to “protect women and support her.”

The Chicago Sky later banned Freedom from home games, although the WNBA didn't issue a league-wide ban.

Earlier this month, Freedom also announced that he intended to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft while claiming to identify as a woman, presenting the move as a challenge to the league’s eligibility framework.

The argument around Freedom has now moved well beyond league policy and into a broader fight over motive, publicity and who is being affected by the debate.

Brink left little ambiguity about her own view. She believes the WNBA is being used as a stage for a controversy that doesn't currently exist on the court, and that the people caught in the middle are members of the transgender community.

articles.title: Stephanie White reveals problem that's stopped Lexie Hull from shining with the Indiana Fever
articles.standfirst: The Fever guard endured four scoreless games, yet defense and lineup impact kept her firmly in starting five
articles.summary: The Fever guard endured four scoreless games, yet defense and lineup impact kept her firmly in starting five
articles.body:
Lexie Hull ’s shooting numbers had become difficult to ignore. Her value to the Indiana Fever had not. That was the message from Stephanie White after Hull delivered one of her best offensive performances in weeks, scoring 14 points on 6-of-8 shooting in Indiana’s 113-90 win over the Chicago Sky .

The performance ended a prolonged cold stretch that included four scoreless WNBA games and no double-digit scoring outing since July 9 against the Phoenix Mercury .

Still, White said the dip in production never changed what she saw from Hull every day.

“Certainly was struggling with confidence, but you could never tell in the way that she shows up,” White said Wednesday. “She’s always going to show up. She’s always going to stay ready.”

Keeping Hull in lineup not about reassurance

The bigger question was why Hull continued starting while her shot disappeared. White made clear that the answer had little to do with trying to restore her confidence.

“Yeah, it’s not to give her reassurance,” White said. “It’s because she impacts us winning, especially on the defensive end of the floor.”

That explains much of Hull ’s importance to Indiana. She's averaging 5.3 points and 3.1 rebounds in 19 minutes per game, modest numbers for a player who has now started 36 straight games after coming off the bench in the first three.

Her role, though, extends well beyond scoring. At 6-foot-1, Hull can take difficult perimeter assignments and give Indiana flexibility around higher-usage guards such as Caitlin Clark and Kelsey Mitchell .

Fever evaluating more than shooting numbers

White also pointed to lineup data and bench construction as part of the decision.

“We look at combinations of players that play together,” she said. “We look at all the analytics just as much as who’s making shots. It’s also important to have punch off the bench and make sure you get production off the bench.

“So really balancing that out, that’s one of the toughest things that you have to do as a coach, constantly evaluating that.”

Sunday’s game showed why the patience could pay off. Hull didn't need to dominate the offense. She simply punished the space Chicago gave her, hitting six of eight shots and two three-pointers while Indiana rolled.

The Fever now turn toward Friday’s home game against the Connecticut Sun , their final contest before the WNBA pauses for the FIBA Women’s World Cup.

Hull’s slump may not be definitively over after one game. Her place in Indiana’s plans, however, appears to have been secure all along.

articles.title: Concerning photo of Caitlin Clark’s arm reveals the brutal toll of WNBA damage
articles.standfirst: Clark delivered a historic 37-point game against Chicago, but a close-up revealed the physical toll behind it
articles.summary: Clark delivered a historic 37-point game against Chicago, but a close-up revealed the physical toll behind it
articles.body:
After pouring in 37 points in the Indiana Fever's dominant 113-90 victory, a close up image of Caitlin Clark began circulating on social media showing her left arm covered in long, visible scratch marks. They were difficult to miss. On a night defined by breathtaking shooting and another piece of WNBA history, the marks on her skin offered a much more painful picture of the physical toll that can come with being one of the league's most closely guarded players.

Clark finished with 37 points , 10 assists and three rebounds while hitting a career-high eight three-pointers on just 12 attempts. The numbers were extraordinary, but perhaps even more remarkable was how routinely she has begun producing them. It was the fifth game of her career with at least 30 points and 10 assists, more than the rest of the WNBA has combined for in league history, according to the Fever.

Caitlin Clark's arm tells a different story

Yet after the final buzzer, it wasn't only Clark's shooting that had people talking. The image of her scratched arm quickly attracted attention, providing a stark contrast to the smiles, highlights and statistics that normally follow a performance like this. The box score showed 37 points. Her arm showed some of the physical punishment that doesn't appear anywhere in those numbers.

That kind of attention is nothing new for Clark. Throughout her first three seasons in the WNBA, defenders have tried to disrupt her rhythm with aggressive pressure, grabs and hard contact.

This season has brought more heated moments , including an incident involving Alyssa Thomas and a recent battle with Paige Bueckers in which the Dallas guard grabbed Clark's arm while trying to draw a foul.

Fever teammate Sophie Cunningham has also earned a reputation for stepping in when the physicality around Clark begins to boil over. It has fueled an ongoing conversation around the Fever star: how much contact is simply part of professional basketball, and when does physical defense cross the line?

Clark rarely needs to say much for that debate to continue. On Sunday, she answered in the way she usually does with the basketball in her hands. Indiana completed a 3-2 road trip, Kelsey Mitchell added 30 points and Chicago was officially eliminated from playoff contention.

But long after the final score, that image remained. Clark's 37 points showed what she was capable of doing to the Sky. The marks across her arm offered a painful glimpse at what she may have absorbed along the way.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark turns her Taylor Swift fandom into a new pair of Nike sneakers
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark’s latest sneaker reveal has Swifties paying attention
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark’s latest sneaker reveal has Swifties paying attention
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark is publicly one of Taylor Swift’s biggest fans. As a Swiftie, the Indiana Fever star did not miss the chance to attend The Eras Tour, and it seems she took plenty of inspiration from the experience to pay tribute to her idol.

Now, with Clark having the freedom to create different versions of her Nike Caitlin 1 line, she took the opportunity to include a pair inspired by the friendship bracelets fans exchanged at Swift’s concerts . Clark revealed the sneakers on her Instagram Stories, and fans immediately noticed the connection to the pop superstar.

A Swiftie touch from the laces to the colors

The design takes the friendship bracelet reference a step further, featuring small charms like in the The Eras Tour. The shoes are mostly white, with stylish, chunky, fuzzy blush-colored laces covered with small beads designed to look like charms.

Clark’s initials, “CC,” appear on the bottom lace of the left shoe, while “22,” her jersey number, sits on the bottom right lace in block-lettered beads. The number could also be a nod to Swift’s song “22.” When the sneakers officially hit the shelves, the Swifties are going to go crazy.

Two influential women, one very unexpected crossover

The collaboration is an iconic one because it brings together two women who lead their respective industries . Swift has established herself as one of the most influential figures in music, while Clark has become one of the most influential athletes of the moment. Their impact has not only been seen in competition among women, but also in breaking numbers and records that were previously associated with men.

Now that Taylor Swift has been embracing sports, it would not be surprising to see her bless the WNBA arenas and support Clark at one of her games . That would certainly be a legendary moment, especially after Clark gave fans a sneak peek at the sneakers and called them “the ones.”

Could Taylor Swift be the next surprise guest courtside?

Swift has already crossed into the sports world while inspiring designs created in her honor, so seeing her at a WNBA game supporting Clark would be another major moment. In 2024, Clark revealed that the pop superstar had sent her four bags of merchandise from her Eras Tour, along with a note saying that Clark was inspiring to watch from afar.

Swift and Clark have also made public appearances together at Kansas City Chiefs football games in support of Swift’s husband, tight end Travis Kelce. They were spotted chatting in a VIP suite during the Chiefs’ Week 6 matchup against the Detroit Lions and later sat together during the 2024 divisional round when Kansas City faced the Houston Texans. So perhaps their next catch-up could happen on a WNBA court.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham pulls down her pants creating the most random moment in front of the camera
articles.standfirst: Sophie Cunningham continues to do things her own way, no matter what people have to say
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham continues to do things her own way, no matter what people have to say
articles.body:
S ophie Cunningham has made it clear that she does not care in the slightest about what people might say about her on social media or in the news. She is focused on being herself, even if one of her moves could potentially earn her a suspension from the Indiana Fever for inappropriate conduct. For many fans, however, it was simply a funny moment that represents exactly who the player is.

Sophie has already been through almost every controversy imaginable, and another one has now been added to the list . Her sense of humor can be sharp at times, but that is also part of why her fan base remains loyal. She is simply herself and stands by what she believes.

Her latest move is already dividing fans

For many, the moment was another example of Cunningham being herself. But for those who oppose her and her ideals, the incident is another reason to call for stronger measures from the league .

During pregame shootaround, Cunningham spotted someone, presumably a team staff member, filming her from the bench. She initially pretended not to notice before slowly pulling down her sweatpants and briefly revealing her backside in compression shorts to the camera.

The video quickly found its way across social media

She quickly pulled her pants back up, then turned around laughing and pointing toward the camera before resuming her warmup . The video is already making the rounds on social media and has undoubtedly created one of the most random moments of the night.

The controversies continue to pile up for Cunningham , but based on this type of attitude, the Indiana Fever star has absolutely nothing to hide — not even her underwear.

articles.title: The Indiana Fever makes ambitious request regarding Sophie Cunningham, which Caitlin Clark also supports
articles.standfirst: The Fever have made their position clear as Cunningham’s breakout bench role fuels an awards push
articles.summary: The Fever have made their position clear as Cunningham’s breakout bench role fuels an awards push
articles.body:
Sophie Cunningham ’s second season with the Indiana Fever has become about far more than simply staying healthy.

After seeing her first year in Indiana cut short by injury, the veteran WNBA guard has returned as one of the league’s most efficient shooters and the Fever now believe she deserves recognition for it.

Ahead of Friday’s home game against the Connecticut Sun , Indiana publicly backed Cunningham for Sixth Player of the Year, making clear how highly the organization values the impact she has made off the bench.

“She gives us the juice when she comes in off the bench,” the Fever posted, before adding: “Sophie Cunningham for 6th Player of the Year.”

The endorsement comes during a season in which Cunningham has become an important part of a high-powered Indiana offense built around Caitlin Clark , Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston .

Through 38 games, Cunningham is averaging 8.4 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.3 assists while shooting 47.6 percent from the field. Her biggest contribution has come from long range, where she has converted 44.1 percent of her three-point attempts and made 63 threes.

That percentage ranks among the best marks in the WNBA and has given Indiana another reliable perimeter threat when its starters need a spark.

Cunningham has built legitimate awards case

Cunningham ’s value has been particularly evident on nights when Indiana has needed secondary scoring.

Her best offensive performance of the season came against the Toronto Tempo on June 16, when she scored 24 points and made six of seven attempts from beyond the arc. The six made three-pointers matched her career high.

She delivered another major shooting performance in a 109-75 victory over the Las Vegas Aces , scoring 20 points while once again making six three-pointers. Cunningham has also produced in high-pressure moments.

Earlier this season against Connecticut , she scored 11 points over the final two minutes, including three 3-pointers, helping Indiana close out an 85-75 victory after the Sun threatened to make the finish uncomfortable.

Those performances have helped transform Cunningham from a useful rotation piece into one of the Fever ’s most dependable options outside their established core.

Fever message comes during record-setting season

Cunningham ’s individual resurgence has unfolded alongside one of the strongest seasons in franchise history. Indiana has reached 25 victories, setting a new franchise record while remaining firmly positioned in the postseason race.

Cunningham ’s ability to stretch defenses has played a meaningful role in that success, particularly when opponents focus their attention on Clark, Mitchell and Boston .

Her personality has also made her one of the team’s most visible players, with another playful pregame interaction going viral this week and adding to her growing profile in Indiana.

The more significant story, however, remains what she has done once the ball is in play.

Friday’s matchup with Connecticut gives Cunningham another opportunity to strengthen her award case against a team she has already punished in a crucial late-game stretch this season.

Tipoff is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET. Indiana has already cast its unofficial vote. The question now is whether the rest of the WNBA will agree.

articles.title: Aliyah Boston reveals Caitlin Clark's struggles when she crosses paths with Angel Reese
articles.standfirst: Boston explained why Fever were hardly surprised when Clark’s reaction became the latest talking point involving Reese
articles.summary: Boston explained why Fever were hardly surprised when Clark’s reaction became the latest talking point involving Reese
articles.body:
Aliyah Boston didn't see Caitlin Clark ’s reaction in real time. Once she saw the clip later, though, the Indiana Fever center knew exactly what was coming.

Clark had already helped Indiana survive a tense 95-91 overtime victory over the Atlanta Dream on August 16 when another moment from the game began spreading across social media.

Angel Reese had missed a potential game-winning putback at the end of regulation, and cameras then caught Clark in the background appearing to smile as Reese stood with her teammates.

The brief reaction quickly became another talking point in a rivalry that has followed Clark and Reese from college basketball into the WNBA .

Boston addressed the moment on the “Post Moves” podcast alongside Candace Parker , admitting the Fever didn't notice anything unusual while the game was actually unfolding.

“We saw it after, but like in real time you see nothing,” Boston said. “We saw it after and I was like, ‘Here we go.’ Just like peace, love and happiness. We will never be free.”

Her response captured the sense that almost any interaction involving Clark and Reese can become a larger story, even when the players themselves may barely register it.

Clark and Reese under constant scrutiny

The attention surrounding Clark and Reese has been relentless since their famous meeting in the 2023 NCAA national championship game, when Reese ’s “you can’t see me” gesture toward Clark became one of the defining images of LSU’s victory over Iowa.

Their move to the WNBA only intensified the focus, and every matchup between them has carried an extra layer of anticipation. The August 16 game offered plenty of basketball drama before the viral clip emerged.

Clark finished with 26 points and nine assists to lead Indiana, while Reese produced 15 points, 14 rebounds and six assists for Atlanta. Reese nearly decided the game in regulation when she grabbed a missed shot from Rhyne Howard and attempted a putback at the rim.

The shot didn't fall, sending the contest to overtime and opening the door for Indiana to finish the job. Parker found Clark ’s reaction amusing and suggested it had produced one of the season’s most memorable memes.

Boston ’s reaction was less about the smile itself and more about what she knew would follow.

“No ‘cause like, we just, peace, love and happiness. We will never be free!” Boston said.

Fever stars magnets for viral moments

Indiana has found itself at the center of several social-media moments this season, something Parker also joked about during the podcast.

She referenced other incidents involving Fever players, including Sophie Cunningham ’s animated gestures and Paige Bueckers telling Clark to calm down.

“I would have been like Paige, too,” Parker said. “I’d have been like, ‘Calm down. I’m trying to foul you.’” Boston wasn't convinced: “No, I don’t care,” she replied.

The Fever have continued pushing forward amid the attention, while Atlanta responded to the loss by putting together a four-game winning streak and securing a playoff berth.

The viral clip may have lasted only seconds, but Boston ’s reaction made it thing clear that Indiana ’s players have become accustomed to everything involving Clark being examined frame by frame.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark and the Fever make the WNBA’s 30th season historic with a feat never seen in league history
articles.standfirst: Nine of the WNBA's 10 most-watched games this season feature Clark and the Indiana Fever
articles.summary: Nine of the WNBA's 10 most-watched games this season feature Clark and the Indiana Fever
articles.body:
After the four Sunday games, the WNBA will enter a break from August 31 through September 16, to accommodate the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, Germany, where 12 of their stars, including Caitlin Clark , A'ja Wilson , and Paige Bueckers , will represent the USA in Group D, facing China on September 4th, Italy on September 6th, and Czechia on September 7th.

When they return, each team will have around four to three games remaining on their schedules, which will primarily serve to determine final positioning since the eight playoff teams are already officially locked in : the Lynx, Valkyries, Aces, Dream, Fever, Liberty, Mystics, and Wings.

Caitlin Clark Shatter WNBA Viewership Records

This season, the league is celebrating its 30th anniversary , and across the 29 previous campaigns, it has never experienced this level of intense media attention or television viewership, a surge driven entirely by the cultural phenomenon of Caitlin Clark .

Historically, the two most-watched games in league history dated back to the inaugural 1997 season , when the opener between the New York Liberty and Los Angeles Sparks drew over 5 million viewers , followed by the Phoenix Mercury versus Charlotte Sting matchup pulling in 3.59 million the next day.

Ranking firmly at number three is the Fever's recent showdown against the Chicago Sky , with NBC reporting that 3.31 million viewers tuned in.

Including this blockbuster affair, three of the WNBA's top ten most-watched broadcasts of all time have occurred this year, every single one featuring the Indiana Fever and Clark, who made history before the season even tipped off by becoming the first team in league history to have 100% of their games televised nationally.

The milestone ratings wave continues down the all-time list, with Fever matchups occupying the sixth and seventh spots for regular-season broadcasts: Indiana's clash against the Aces drew 2.64 million viewers , while their battle against the Dream brought in 2.60 million .

Following tonight's contest against the Connecticut Sun, an opponent sitting near the bottom of the league standings, the Fever will play four remaining regular-season games, capped by a heavyweight back-to-back series against the league-leading Minnesota Lynx .

Given the massive national spotlight, those late-season clashes stand a strong chance of crashing the all-time top-ten viewership chart as Clark and her squad rewrite the business side of professional basketball.

articles.title: Seattle Storm rookie Awa Fam, from Spain, embodies the vision the WNBA wants to showcase to the world
articles.standfirst: The Spanish rookie is part of a new generation connecting the WNBA with the global game
articles.summary: The Spanish rookie is part of a new generation connecting the WNBA with the global game
articles.body:
Awa Fam’s first season in the WNBA hasn’t unfolded perfectly for the Seattle Storm , but the Spanish rookie has offered a compelling glimpse of what the league’s future could look like.

Selected No. 3 overall by Seattle in the 2026 WNBA Draft, Fam entered the league as one of the most promising young players in international basketball.

At 6-foot-4, she brings size, mobility and versatility to the court, but it’s her unusual path to the WNBA that makes her particularly significant.

Fam didn’t take the familiar American route through college basketball. Instead, she began playing professional basketball in Spain at just 15 years old, joining Valencia Basket and becoming the youngest player to appear for the club’s top team.

While many players her age were still focused entirely on school and youth basketball, Fam was traveling across Europe to compete against experienced professionals.

“I was 15 years old playing against 30-year-old girls,” Fam recalled, describing the experience as a crazy life.

That early exposure helped prepare her for the demands of professional basketball and eventually made her transition to Seattle considerably smoother.

Because she remained with Valencia for its Liga Femenina playoffs after being drafted, the Storm used video calls with assistant coaches to help her prepare for life in the WNBA.

Fam made an immediate impression when she finally joined Seattle. She scored 10 points in her WNBA debut against the Washington Mystics on May 24, shooting 4-for-7 from the field. Less than two weeks later, she became the youngest player in Storm history to start a game.

Her rookie campaign has also put her alongside a promising young Seattle core that includes 2025 No. 2 pick Dominique Malonga and fellow rookie Fla’Jae Johnson.

Despite the Storm’s difficult season, Fam has emerged as one of the team’s encouraging building blocks.

Fam is becoming part of a global WNBA

Now, her attention turns back to Spain and the international stage. Fam is representing her country at the 2026 FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup in Berlin, Germany, which begins Sept. 4.

Spain will face Japan, Mali and host Germany in Group A, giving Fam another opportunity to compete against elite players from around the world.

Her participation also highlights how closely connected the WNBA has become with international basketball.

Seattle has three players involved in the tournament, with Ezi Magbegor and Jade Melbourne representing Australia and Dominique Malonga playing for France. Across the tournament, WNBA talent will be spread throughout numerous national teams.

That growing international presence fits the league’s broader ambitions. WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert has identified global growth as an important part of what comes next for the league, and the 2026 draft itself underscored the expanding international pipeline.

Fam’s temporary contract suspension with Seattle allows her to represent Spain before returning to the Storm following the tournament. It’s a fitting arrangement for a player whose career has always crossed borders.

Fam represents the increasingly fluid relationship between European basketball and the WNBA, and could become one of the young faces of the league’s global future.

articles.title: Simone Biles makes no secret of her support for Caitlin Clark during the recent Indiana Fever game
articles.standfirst: The Olympic champion was in attendance for a night that ended with a spectacular performance from the Indiana Fever star.
articles.summary: The Olympic champion was in attendance for a night that ended with a spectacular performance from the Indiana Fever star.
articles.body:
Simone Biles did not want to miss the opportunity to experience the WNBA up close and made an appearance at Gainbridge Fieldhouse to watch the matchup between the Indiana Fever and Connecticut Sun . The gymnast shared part of her night on social media, making her support for Clark clear.

A post with a detail that did not go unnoticed

Biles shared different moments from her visit to the arena. In one photo, she appeared holding a basketball, while another showed her outfit for the occasion, featuring a WNBA Essentials sweatshirt, black boots, a white handbag and her braids.

But a third image carried a different kind of significance.

In the photo, Clark can be seen from behind, a detail that once again highlighted the closeness and support Biles has shown toward the Indiana star on different occasions.

And while that image began drawing attention away from the court, Clark had a performance of her own waiting inside the arena that ultimately became the night's main attraction.

Caitlin Clark answered with a spectacular performance

The Indiana Fever star was one of the biggest reasons the night ended in the home team's favor.

Clark finished the game with 34 points and 12 assists in 33 minutes, recording a double-double while leading her team's offensive production . Her performance became one of the defining moments of the victory and once again showed the impact she can have when she controls the pace of the game.

Her individual performance became even more impressive considering the margin Indiana was able to build throughout the matchup.

Indiana Fever dominated from start to finish

The final score reflected Fever's superiority.

Indiana defeated the Connecticut Sun 111-91 , earning a convincing victory and closing this first stage of the season with a 26-14 record.

Beyond the team's numbers, the result allowed Indiana to remain among the higher-ranked teams in the standings, while Clark's performance provided the individual finishing touch to a night that had already attracted attention from the stands.

articles.title: Nike bows to Caitlin Clark with powerful message after historic WNBA feat
articles.standfirst: Clark keeps on shining and dominating the WNBA
articles.summary: Clark keeps on shining and dominating the WNBA
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark has given Nike another reason to celebrate after producing a statistical first in WNBA history.

The Indiana Fever star followed one huge performance with another against the Connecticut Sun , becoming the first player in league history to record consecutive games with at least 30 points and 10 assists.

Nike responded almost immediately with a four-word message on X.

“How to stop@caitlinclark22,” the company wrote, linking the post to the Merriam Webster definition of “impossible.”

Nike reacts after Clark makes history

Clark's latest performance included 34 points, 12 assists, five rebounds and three steals , while she also connected on six three-pointers.

She shot 12 of 19 from the field and finished with a game-high plus-32 as Indiana strengthened its position in the standings.

The milestone was completed just five days after Clark had scored 37 points and supplied 10 assists against the Chicago Sky .

That two-game stretch also made her only the seventh player in WNBA history to record consecutive 30-point double-doubles.

Clark wasn't the only Fever player producing huge numbers against Connecticut.

Kelsey Mitchell also scored 34 points on 12 of 19 shooting, marking the fourth time this season that she and Clark have each scored at least 30 points in the same game.

That is already a single-season WNBA record.

Clark's Nike partnership takes another step

The timing of Nike's reaction was notable because Clark had only recently unveiled another version of her signature sneaker.

The Nike Caitlin 1 “Friendship Bracelet” was revealed two days before the Connecticut game, and Clark had already expressed her excitement about the design.

“Probably some of the ones that I was the most excited about,” Clark said before the game.

“Obviously I had the Kobe version, but I feel like these are even better, and it’ll come with some charms that everybody can pick and kind of make your own.”

Indiana had to recover from a 14-point deficit before taking control, closing the first half with an 18-2 run and carrying a 58-43 lead into halftime.

The win moved the Fever to 26-14 and lifted them to fourth in the standings.

Clark now turns her attention toward international duty with Team USA in Berlin, but Nike's reaction showed just how quickly another historic WNBA performance had captured attention.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark gets backing from NFL legend Ryan Clark amid WNBA tensions
articles.standfirst: Ryan Clark wants the league to focus on its players rather than off-court controversies.
articles.summary: Ryan Clark wants the league to focus on its players rather than off-court controversies.
articles.body:
NFL legend Ryan Clark has called on the WNBA to publicly support Caitlin Clark and other players as debates away from basketball continue to dominate discussion around the league.

Speaking on The Pivot podcast, Clark argued that attention should return to the women actually competing rather than controversies surrounding the WNBA.

“The biggest thing to me is the WNBA needs to take a stand and say they stand with the women that are on the court right now playing. That is who they want to protect. And we should stop having conversations about a make-believe issue that the WNBA has not had in 30 years of its existence,” Clark said.

Ryan Clark wants Caitlin Clark's basketball to take center stage

Clark specifically pointed towards Caitlin Clark's performances as an example of what he believes should be generating headlines.

“What you should be talking about the fact that Sydney Taylor has gone from undrafted player to clutch bucket maker in the most important moments for her team. That Natasha Cloud, just three games before the incident happened, had 35 points and she was looking for a team this offseason,” Clark added.

“Caitlin Clark on that very night hit eight three-pointers. This is somebody that’s in the MVP conversations, one of the faces of the league.”

The comments come as Caitlin Clark continues to find herself at the center of wider arguments involving officiating, physical play and political debates surrounding the WNBA.

NBA commissioner Adam Silver recently defended her publicly.

Ryan Clark urges WNBA to celebrate its stars

“I have come to know Caitlin really well,” Silver said.

“She’s an incredible player and also an incredible person. And she wants to focus on being the best player she can. She has become a bit of a political football in this country, and I think it’s incredibly unfair to her.”

Ryan Clark believes the same problem is preventing other WNBA players from receiving recognition for their achievements.

“And instead of talking about uplifting her and her game, you’re now dealing with nonsense and having to have conversations about that. Angel Reese goes for 31 points two games ago, has 26 rebounds in the next game to break a record. You’ve been fighting all this time for those sorts of people to be recognized.”

His message is ultimately that Caitlin Clark and her fellow WNBA stars should be discussed primarily for what they are producing on the court.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark delivers a historic week no WNBA player has ever matched strengthening her MVP case
articles.standfirst: Clark is having the most productive offensive season ever, with the most combined assists and points
articles.summary: Clark is having the most productive offensive season ever, with the most combined assists and points
articles.body:
After this Sunday games the WNBA is entering a short break from August 31 through September 16 due to the FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup in Berlin, Germany.

When the action returns, each squad will have roughly three to four games remaining on their schedules that will serve a dual purpose; first, to lock down final seeding in the standings since the eight playoff participants (Lynx, Valkyries, Aces, Dream, Fever, Liberty, Mystics, and Wings) have already clinched their postseason berths.

The second priority centers on major individual honors, where rookie sensation Olivia Miles has all but locked up Rookie of the Year , while the MVP race has narrowed down to a fierce two-player battle between four-time winner A'ja Wilson , who is also tracking toward her fourth Defensive Player of the Year award, and Caitlin Clark , whose unprecedented offensive production accounts for a staggering 41.4 points created per game , standing as the highest mark in league history backed by 22.5 PPG and a league-leading 8.4 APG .

Caitlin Clark Rewrite the WNBA Record Books

The offensive explosion coming out of Indiana this season has been entirely unprecedented, averaging 97.0 PPG , the highest single-season scoring average in league history, and following up with their 19th game scoring 100 or more points in a dominant 111-91 victory over Connecticut.

In that stellar performance, Caitlin Clark and backcourt partner Kelsey Mitchell each poured in 34 points, marking a record fourth time the dynamic duo has both eclipsed the 30-point mark in the same contest.

For Mitchell, it marked her 24th consecutive game scoring 20 or more points, extending her WNBA record, while Clark finished her night with 34 points and 12 assists.

This accomplishment made her the first player in league history to register back-to-back games with 30+ points and 10+ assists , further solidifying a campaign where she became the first player ever to record 800+ points and 300+ assists in a single season, alongside clearing 100+ three-pointers.

This stellar bounce-back year following her limited 13-game action in 2025 has been nothing short of extraordinary, placing her squarely alongside Wilson in the thick of the MVP conversation . When professional play resumes following the international window, the Fever will play their final four regular-season games, capped by a high-stakes back-to-back series against the league-leading Minnesota Lynx.

articles.title: Stephanie White defends Caitlin Clark after the Indiana Fever star finished behind A’ja Wilson in the latest ESPN poll
articles.standfirst: Clark responds to her No. 2 ranking with another record-setting performance that strengthens her case among the WNBA’s elite
articles.summary: Clark responds to her No. 2 ranking with another record-setting performance that strengthens her case among the WNBA’s elite
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark continues to produce performances that would represent career nights for most players, but Indiana Fever head coach Stephanie White believes the guard’s brilliance is becoming surprisingly easy to overlook.

Clark delivered another sensational performance on Friday, scoring 34 points and recording 12 assists as the Fever defeated the Connecticut Sun 111-91.

She shot 12-of-19 from the field, added five rebounds, six 3-pointers and three steals, and needed only 34 minutes to put together another remarkable stat line.

White believes Clark’s ability to make difficult plays appear effortless is one reason her achievements can sometimes be taken for granted.

“You watch her, and I think it’s easy to take for granted some of the things that she does,” White said after the game. She added that great players have a way of making complicated aspects of the game look simple, calling what Clark is doing “really special.”

The timing of Clark’s latest performance was notable because it came shortly after ESPN’s latest player ranking.

The three-time All-Star was voted the second-best player in the WNBA, finishing behind Las Vegas Aces superstar A’ja Wilson , who remains one of the leading MVP candidates this season.

While Wilson’s position at No. 1 is understandable, Clark’s recent production continues to strengthen the argument surrounding her place among the league’s elite.

Clark’s latest outing added another extraordinary chapter to her young career

She recorded the sixth 30-point, 10-assist game of her WNBA career, giving her more such performances than any other player in league history. She also became the first player in WNBA history to post 800 or more points and 300 or more assists in a single season.

Her latest accomplishment comes after she became the first player to reach 300 assists and 100 made 3-pointers in a season.

Yet Clark wasn’t particularly interested in celebrating her individual statistics following the win.

“I mean, I don’t really care about the stats,” Clark said, explaining that when she’s playing freely and finding her rhythm, the numbers tend to follow naturally.

Clark also emphasized that her production is most valuable when it helps the Fever succeed collectively. Her ability to make shots and find open teammates can generate momentum throughout the lineup.

That was evident against Connecticut, with Kelsey Mitchell matching Clark’s 34 points and Aliyah Boston contributing 14. The Fever’s starters combined for an outstanding offensive display as Indiana secured another convincing victory.

The win improved Indiana’s record to 26-14 and moved the Fever into fourth place with four regular-season games remaining. Their remaining schedule won’t be easy, with three of those games coming against playoff teams and the final two against the Minnesota Lynx.

The bigger picture remains clear for Clark . She believes there’s still plenty of room for improvement, despite already rewriting several WNBA records.

If anything, the fact that a 34-point double-double can feel almost routine is perhaps the clearest indication of how special Clark has become.

articles.title: Simone Biles receives huge ovation at Fever game before sharing special moment with Caitlin Clark on historic night
articles.standfirst: One of the greatest athletes of all time came to watch, but by the end of the night there was plenty of admiration going both ways
articles.summary: One of the greatest athletes of all time came to watch, but by the end of the night there was plenty of admiration going both ways
articles.body:
S imone Biles knows what it feels like when an arena stops to recognize greatness. She has heard those roars after Olympic medals, impossible routines and moments that changed gymnastics forever. On Friday night in Indianapolis, she wasn't competing at all. She was simply sitting in the stands when thousands of people made sure she knew exactly what she still means to them.

When Biles appeared on the giant screen at Gainbridge Fieldhouse during the Indiana Fever's game against the Connecticut Sun, the crowd erupted. The most decorated gymnast in history smiled and waved back as the cheers poured down. It was a beautiful reception for an American sporting icon, but the night was about to produce another moment that felt just as special.

Because while Biles was watching from the stands, Caitlin Clark was making history on the court.

Clark delivered 34 points and 12 assists as Indiana overwhelmed Connecticut 111-91, while Kelsey Mitchell added 34 points of her own. Clark became the first player in WNBA history to record at least 800 points and 300 assists in a single season. She also became the first to combine 300 assists with at least 100 made three-pointers in a season.

Simone Biles and Caitlin Clark share a moment away from the crowd

But one of the most memorable images of the night didn't happen in front of thousands of screaming fans.

After the game, Biles made her way into the hallway outside the Fever locker room, where the Olympic legend and Clark finally came face-to-face that night. They smiled, embraced and Clark greeted her warmly with a simple, “Good to see you.”

Biles also spent time greeting other members of the Fever. She exchanged hugs and smiles with Kelsey Mitchell, Lexie Hull, Aliyah Boston and other Indiana players, while Sophie Cunningham gave the gymnastics legend an especially enthusiastic welcome, telling her, “You are a badass.” Biles was accompanied by her brother during the postgame visit.

The admiration clearly went both ways. Biles may own seven Olympic gold medals and more World Championship medals than any gymnast in history, but she wasn't walking through that hallway asking to be treated like royalty. She was there as a sports fan, congratulating another group of women for what they had just accomplished.

Biles attended her first WNBA game at the same arena exactly two years earlier, on August 28, 2024, when Indiana also faced Connecticut. That night, Clark broke the WNBA rookie record for three-pointers in a season. Afterward, Biles met the Fever players and celebrated women's sports, while Clark admitted she was having her own fangirl moment over meeting the Olympic superstar.

Two years later, Biles came back. And once again, Clark made history with her watching.

This time Clark wasn't a rookie discovering the league anymore. She was the player who had just produced 34 points and 12 assists, helped Indiana win for the seventh time in nine games and put together statistical combinations no player in WNBA history had ever reached.

For a few seconds in that hallway, though, none of those numbers seemed particularly important.

It was simply Simone Biles and Caitlin Clark smiling and embracing, two of the biggest names in American sports sharing a moment of genuine mutual admiration.
paragraphs: S imone Biles knows what it feels like when an arena stops to recognize greatness. She has heard those roars after Olympic medals, impossible routines and moments that changed gymnastics forever. On Friday night in Indianapolis, she wasn't competing at all. She was simply sitting in the stands when thousands of people made sure she knew exactly what she still means to them.

When Biles appeared on the giant screen at Gainbridge Fieldhouse during the Indiana Fever's game against the Connecticut Sun, the crowd erupted. The most decorated gymnast in history smiled and waved back as the cheers poured down. It was a beautiful reception for an American sporting icon, but the night was about to produce another moment that felt just as special.
Because while Biles was watching from the stands, Caitlin Clark was making history on the court.

Clark delivered 34 points and 12 assists as Indiana overwhelmed Connecticut 111-91, while Kelsey Mitchell added 34 points of her own. Clark became the first player in WNBA history to record at least 800 points and 300 assists in a single season. She also became the first to combine 300 assists with at least 100 made three-pointers in a season.
Simone Biles and Caitlin Clark share a moment away from the crowd
But one of the most memorable images of the night didn't happen in front of thousands of screaming fans.

After the game, Biles made her way into the hallway outside the Fever locker room, where the Olympic legend and Clark finally came face-to-face that night. They smiled, embraced and Clark greeted her warmly with a simple, “Good to see you.”

Biles also spent time greeting other members of the Fever. She exchanged hugs and smiles with Kelsey Mitchell, Lexie Hull, Aliyah Boston and other Indiana players, while Sophie Cunningham gave the gymnastics legend an especially enthusiastic welcome, telling her, “You are a badass.” Biles was accompanied by her brother during the postgame visit.

The admiration clearly went both ways. Biles may own seven Olympic gold medals and more World Championship medals than any gymnast in history, but she wasn't walking through that hallway asking to be treated like royalty. She was there as a sports fan, congratulating another group of women for what they had just accomplished.

Biles attended her first WNBA game at the same arena exactly two years earlier, on August 28, 2024, when Indiana also faced Connecticut. That night, Clark broke the WNBA rookie record for three-pointers in a season. Afterward, Biles met the Fever players and celebrated women's sports, while Clark admitted she was having her own fangirl moment over meeting the Olympic superstar.
Two years later, Biles came back. And once again, Clark made history with her watching.

This time Clark wasn't a rookie discovering the league anymore. She was the player who had just produced 34 points and 12 assists, helped Indiana win for the seventh time in nine games and put together statistical combinations no player in WNBA history had ever reached.
For a few seconds in that hallway, though, none of those numbers seemed particularly important.
It was simply Simone Biles and Caitlin Clark smiling and embracing, two of the biggest names in American sports sharing a moment of genuine mutual admiration.

articles.title: The wig is back: Royce White shows up courtside at the Fever game despite the WNBA ban
articles.standfirst: Former NBA player doubles down on controversial WNBA campaign
articles.summary: Former NBA player doubles down on controversial WNBA campaign
articles.body:
Royce White has taken his unusual campaign for a place in the WNBA straight to the sidelines.

The former NBA first-round pick arrived at Gainbridge Fieldhouse on Friday night to watch the Indiana Fever face the Connecticut Sun, but he wasn't dressed like an ordinary courtside spectator.

White wore a long blonde wig and embraced the character he has created as part of his controversial push to enter the 2027 WNBA Draft.

The Fever ultimately cruised to a 111-91 victory over Connecticut, but White's appearance generated plenty of attention away from the action on the court.

White also posted about his appearance on Instagram, where he referred to himself as “Queen Roysha” and used deliberately provocative language while discussing his identity.

“The Kweeeen has arrived! They better bow for a beautiful Black Trans Lesbian!,” White wrote.

The timing was particularly notable because the WNBA has reportedly already ruled White and former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom ineligible for the 2027 draft. Both men had announced plans to enter the league while saying they identify as women.

League sources told Reuters that neither is eligible, although the WNBA hasn't publicly laid out a detailed explanation for the individual decisions.

White's original draft declaration was submitted to the league through his attorney, former Florida congressman Matt Gaetz . Since then, he has continued to publicize his campaign rather than backing away after the reported ruling.

White's courtside appearance follows Kanter Freedom controversy

White's decision to attend the Fever game also comes shortly after Kanter Freedom became involved in a confrontation at another Indiana game.

Kanter Freedom was at the Fever's Aug. 23 matchup with the Chicago Sky at Wintrust Arena when he became involved in a heated exchange with Sky guard Natasha Cloud . Security eventually removed him from the arena during the third quarter.

The Chicago Sky later banned him from attending games at the venue, with team owner Michael Alter describing him as a potential threat.

The incident added to the publicity campaign being pursued by the two former NBA players. Their actions have drawn strong reactions from members of the WNBA, including Cloud and Los Angeles Sparks center Cameron Brink.

Brink publicly criticized Kanter Freedom after his ejection, accusing him of targeting the transgender community.

White , meanwhile, appears determined to keep the controversy visible. His blonde-wig appearance in Indianapolis gave him another opportunity to turn the draft dispute into a public spectacle, even though his reported ineligibility means he won't be joining the Fever or another WNBA team through the 2027 draft.

White's latest courtside appearance suggests he isn't planning to let the WNBA's reported decision end the conversation.
